# Claude models in Microsoft Foundry

Anthropic's Claude models bring advanced conversational AI capabilities to Microsoft Foundry, providing state-of-the-art language understanding and generation for intelligent applications. Claude models excel at complex reasoning, code generation, and multimodal tasks including image analysis. This article describes the available Claude models, how they're hosted and billed, supported APIs, capabilities, and best practices.

To deploy and call a Claude model, see Deploy and use Claude models in Microsoft Foundry.

Important

Items marked preview in this article are currently in preview. This preview is provided without a service-level agreement, and Microsoft doesn't recommend it for production workloads. Certain features might not be supported or might have constrained capabilities. For more information, see Supplemental Terms of Use for Microsoft Azure Previews.

## How Claude models are hosted and billed

Microsoft Foundry offers Claude models in two versions:

- Version 1: Hosted on Anthropic infrastructure; these models run on Anthropic's infrastructure (outside of Azure).
- Version 2: Hosted on Azure; these models run on Azure infrastructure end-to-end and are all Generally available (GA).

Not all models are available in both versions. A model's lifecycle stage, such as Preview or Generally available, can differ between the two versions. For per-model availability and lifecycle status, see Available Claude models.

To compare both hosting options across data residency, SLAs, support paths, compliance, and purchasing flow, see Compare Azure-hosted and Anthropic-hosted Claude models.

Note

You access Claude models in Microsoft Foundry through Foundry Models from partners and community. Models from partners and community that Anthropic sells and operates are Non-Microsoft Products under the Product Terms.

Claude models in Foundry require an Azure Marketplace subscription and bill through Claude Consumption Units (CCU). Ensure that you have the permissions required to subscribe to model offerings before you deploy. For pricing details, see Claude Consumption Units (CCU) billing in Microsoft Foundry.

## Available Claude models

Important

The following Claude models comply with the EU watermarking standard: See Claude Support for model details.

- Interwoven text watermarking (second key): a second key is added for interwoven watermark detection per EU standards. Watermarking happens server-side at generation time; there is no change to request or response shapes.
- C2PA watermarking: C2PA content-provenance marking, handled server/client-side by Anthropic surfaces. No API shape change.

The following table compares model availability for both versions of Claude models in Foundry. For details on the features referenced in the table, see the Capabilities and advanced features section.

For errors you might encounter when you deploy or call Claude models, see Deploy and use Claude models: Troubleshooting.

Anthropic.content:
Compare which Claude Code features work on each Anthropic subscription plan, the Anthropic Console, and cloud providers such as Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud.

The Claude Code CLI and everything that runs locally work on every provider. For setup instructions per provider, see the Enterprise deployment overview. To skip straight to what is missing on your provider, see the summary by provider tabs.In the tables below, ✓ means available, ✗ means not available, and “See note” links to a footnote for partial support. A qualifier after ✓ narrows availability to that subset, and “Admin-enabled” means the feature is off until an organization admin turns it on.

Availability by model provider

How you authenticate determines which features Claude Code can reach. For a single list of what is missing on your provider, see the summary by provider tabs. To find your column in the tables:

Claude subscription: you sign in with a claude.ai account on the Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, or Enterprise plan

MCP servers: connectors from claude.ai load only when your claude.ai subscription is the active authentication method. Tool search isn’t supported on Microsoft Foundry deployments hosted on Azure. On Google Cloud (Google managed), tool search isn’t supported on models earlier than Claude Opus 4.5, Claude Sonnet 4.5, and Claude Haiku 4.5

Subagents: when the parent conversation runs Fable, the built-in Explore subagent runs on Opus with a Claude subscription, an Anthropic Console account, or an LLM gateway reached through ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. On other providers, including Claude Platform on AWS, it runs on Fable

1 On Google Cloud (Google managed), web search is available for Opus 4, Sonnet 4, Haiku 4.5, and later models. 2 On these providers, auto mode supports only Claude Sonnet 5 or later, Opus 4.7 or later, Haiku 5.5, and the Fable models. See Auto mode configuration. For the permission mode a session on these providers starts in, see Which mode a session starts in. 3 Subject to your agreement with the cloud provider. 4 Dashboard and API only. Contribution metrics requires a claude.ai Team or Enterprise organization. 5 Requires Claude Code v2.1.224 or later on macOS and Linux, including Linux inside WSL 2. On native Windows, requires Claude Code v2.1.234 or later. With API key authentication, messaging is same-machine only. On Amazon Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Google Cloud (Anthropic managed), Google Cloud (Google managed), and Microsoft Foundry, messaging is same-machine only and requires Claude Code v2.1.248 or later. Claude can find your cloud sessions and your sessions on other machines only from a session that is connected to Remote Control. To connect, you need a claude.ai sign-in and the other Remote Control requirements. See Message sessions on other machines.

If you authenticate through an LLM gateway, feature availability matches the underlying provider the gateway forwards to, except for the features Claude Code itself turns off. Whenever ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL points at a host other than api.anthropic.com, Claude Code turns off features such as Remote Control, whatever the gateway forwards. Some features, such as the Advisor, work only if the gateway forwards requests intact.For how the requests Claude Code sends differ between an Amazon Bedrock- or Agent Platform-format gateway, an ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL gateway, and a Claude apps gateway sign-in, see client behavior by connection method.

Summary by provider

Each tab lists what is unavailable or partially supported on that provider, with alternatives where one exists. See also the provider-specific differences. On Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud (Google managed), Microsoft Foundry, and Claude Platform on AWS, error reporting and telemetry to Anthropic are off by default. See default behaviors by API provider for what traffic still reaches Anthropic and how to opt out.

If you authenticate through a cloud provider or an Anthropic Console API key, this section does not apply to you. When you sign in with a claude.ai account, your plan determines which of the features below are available.In Enterprise organizations with the HIPAA configuration applied, some features in this table are turned off.

Ultra is the new name for the Max 20x plan, and Max is the new name for Max 5x. To check which plan you’re on, see your subscription on claude.ai.In Claude Code, Max and Ultra have the same features, listed in the Max and Ultra columns of the availability table. For usage limits and pricing, see the Claude pricing page.

Model availability

For which Claude models and context-window sizes are available per provider and region, see Model configuration and the Models overview. Vision, PDF input, and extended thinking are model capabilities rather than Claude Code features and work on every provider that offers the model. Prompt caching works the same way on most providers; on Amazon Bedrock, support varies by model.

Anthropic.content:
# Customer support agent

## Prerequisites

To follow this guide, you need:

- A Claude API key (set as theANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable)
- Python 3.10 or later

Install the required packages:
pip install anthropic streamlit python-dotenv

## Before building with Claude

### Decide whether to use Claude for support chat

Here are some key indicators that you should employ an LLM such as Claude to automate portions of your customer support process:

### High volume of repetitive queries
Claude excels at handling a large number of similar questions efficiently, freeing up human agents for more complex issues.

### Need for quick information synthesis
Claude can quickly retrieve, process, and combine information from vast knowledge bases, whereas human agents might need time to research or consult multiple sources.

### 24/7 availability requirement
Claude can provide support at all hours without fatigue, whereas staffing human agents for continuous coverage can be costly and challenging.

### Rapid scaling during peak periods
Claude can handle sudden increases in query volume without the need for hiring and training additional staff.

### Consistent brand voice
You can instruct Claude to consistently represent your brand’s tone and values, whereas human agents might vary in their communication styles.

Some considerations for choosing Claude over other LLMs:

- You prioritize natural, nuanced conversation: Claude’s sophisticated language understanding allows for more natural, context-aware conversations that feel more human-like than chats with other LLMs.
- You often receive complex and open-ended queries: Claude can handle a wide range of topics and inquiries without generating scripted responses or requiring extensive programming of permutations of user utterances.
- You need scalable multilingual support: Claude’s multilingual capabilities allow it to engage in conversations in over 200 languages without the need for separate chatbots or extensive translation processes for each supported language.

### Define your ideal chat interaction

Outline an ideal customer interaction to define how and when you expect the customer to interact with Claude. This outline will help to determine the technical requirements of your solution.

Here is an example chat interaction for car insurance customer support:

Customer: Initiates support chat experience

- Claude: Warmly greets customer and initiates conversation

Customer: Asks about insurance for their new electric car

- Claude: Provides relevant information about electric vehicle coverage

Customer: Asks questions related to unique needs for electric vehicle insurance

- Claude: Responds with accurate and informative answers and provides links to the sources

Customer: Asks off-topic questions unrelated to insurance or cars

- Claude: Clarifies it does not discuss unrelated topics and steers the user back to car insurance

Customer: Expresses interest in an insurance quote

- Claude: Asks a set of questions to determine the appropriate quote, adapting to their responses
- Claude: Sends a request to use the quote generation API tool along with necessary information collected from the user
- Claude: Receives the response information from the API tool use, synthesizes the information into a natural response, and presents the provided quote to the user

Customer: Asks follow-up questions

- Claude: Answers follow-up questions as needed
- Claude: Guides the customer to the next steps in the insurance process and closes out the conversation

In the real example that you write for your own use case, you might find it useful to write the actual words in this interaction so that you can also get a sense of the ideal tone, response length, and level of detail you want Claude to have.

### Break the interaction into unique tasks

Customer support chat is a collection of multiple different tasks, from question answering to information retrieval to taking action on requests, wrapped up in a single customer interaction. Before you start building, break down your ideal customer interaction into every task you want Claude to be able to perform. This ensures you can prompt and evaluate Claude for every task, and gives you a good sense of the range of interactions you need to account for when writing test cases.

Customers sometimes find it helpful to visualize this as an interaction flowchart of possible conversation inflection points depending on user requests.

Here are the key tasks associated with the example insurance interaction:

Greeting and general guidance

- Warmly greet the customer and initiate conversation
- Provide general information about the company and interaction

Product information

Provide information about electric vehicle coverage This will require that Claude have the necessary information in its context, and might imply that a

is necessary.

Answer questions related to unique electric vehicle insurance needs

Answer follow-up questions about the quote or insurance details

Offer links to sources when appropriate

Conversation management

- Stay on topic (car insurance)
- Redirect off-topic questions back to relevant subjects

Quote generation

- Ask appropriate questions to determine quote eligibility
- Adapt questions based on customer responses
- Submit collected information to quote generation API
- Present the provided quote to the customer

### Establish success criteria

Work with your support team to define success criteria and write detailed evaluations with measurable benchmarks and goals.

Here are criteria and benchmarks that can be used to evaluate how successfully Claude performs the defined tasks:

### Query comprehension accuracy
This metric evaluates how accurately Claude interprets customer inquiries across various topics. Measure this by reviewing a sample of conversations and assessing whether Claude has the correct interpretation of customer intent, critical next steps, what successful resolution looks like, and more. Aim for a comprehension accuracy of 95 percent or higher.

### Response relevance
This assesses how well Claude’s response addresses the customer’s specific question or issue. Evaluate a set of conversations and rate the relevance of each response (using LLM-based grading for scale). Target a relevance score of 90 percent or above.

### Response accuracy
Assess the correctness of general company and product information provided to the user, based on the information provided to Claude in context. Target 100 percent accuracy in this introductory information.

### Citation provision relevance
Track the frequency and relevance of links or sources offered. Target providing relevant sources in 80 percent of interactions where additional information could be beneficial.

### Topic adherence
Measure how well Claude stays on topic, such as the topic of car insurance in the example implementation. Aim for 95 percent of responses to be directly related to car insurance or the customer’s specific query.

### Content generation effectiveness
Measure how successful Claude is at determining when to generate informational content and how relevant that content is. For example, in this implementation, you would be determining how well Claude identifies when to generate a quote and how accurate that quote is. Target 100 percent accuracy, as this is vital information for a successful customer interaction.

### Escalation efficiency
This measures Claude’s ability to recognize when a query needs human intervention and escalate appropriately. Track the percentage of correctly escalated conversations versus those that should have been escalated but weren’t. Aim for an escalation accuracy of 95 percent or higher.

Here are criteria and benchmarks that can be used to evaluate the business impact of employing Claude for support:

### Sentiment maintenance
This assesses Claude’s ability to maintain or improve customer sentiment throughout the conversation. Use sentiment analysis tools to measure sentiment at the beginning and end of each conversation. Aim for maintained or improved sentiment in 90 percent of interactions.

### Deflection rate
The percentage of customer inquiries successfully handled by the chatbot without human intervention. Typically aim for a 70–80 percent deflection rate, depending on the complexity of inquiries.

### Customer satisfaction score
A measure of how satisfied customers are with their chatbot interaction. Usually done through post-interaction surveys. Aim for a CSAT score of 4 out of 5 or higher.

### Average handle time
The average time it takes for the chatbot to resolve an inquiry. This varies widely based on the complexity of issues, but generally, aim for a lower AHT compared to human agents.

### Choose the right Claude model

The choice of model depends on the trade-offs among cost, accuracy, and response time.

For customer support chat, Claude Opus 5.5 is well suited to balance intelligence, latency, and cost, including the most complex support scenarios that require deep reasoning across long, multistep conversations. However, for instances where you have a conversation flow with multiple prompts including RAG, tool use, or long-context prompts, Claude Haiku 5.5 might be more suitable to optimize for latency. Effort is its main control for speed:low is the fastest level, suited to chat and short tool tasks.

### Build a strong prompt

Anthropic.title: Glossary
Anthropic.description: The Claude API does not currently offer fine-tuning, but ask your Anthropic contact if you are interested in exploring this option. ... Claude, an AI assistant for life and work built by Anthropic, is based on a large language model that has been fine-tuned and trained using RLHF.
Anthropic.content:
# Glossary

## Context window

The “context window” refers to the amount of text a language model can look back on and reference when generating new text. This is different from the large corpus of data the language model was trained on, and instead represents a “working memory” for the model. A larger context window allows the model to process and respond to more complex and lengthy prompts, whereas a smaller context window might limit the model’s ability to handle longer prompts or maintain coherence over extended conversations.

See the guide to understanding context windows to learn more.

## Fine-tuning

Fine-tuning is the process of further training a pretrained language model using additional data. This causes the model to start representing and mimicking the patterns and characteristics of the fine-tuning dataset. Claude is not a bare language model; it has already been fine-tuned to be a helpful assistant. The Claude API does not currently offer fine-tuning, but ask your Anthropic contact if you are interested in exploring this option. Fine-tuning can be useful for adapting a language model to a specific domain, task, or writing style, but it requires careful consideration of the fine-tuning data and the potential impact on the model’s performance and biases.

## HHH

HHH (helpful, honest, harmless) is a research framework that informs how Claude is trained to be beneficial to society. It is distinct from the Claude product tagline, “AI assistant for life and work.”

- A helpful AI will attempt to perform the task or answer the question posed to the best of its abilities, providing relevant and useful information.
- An honest AI will give accurate information, and not hallucinate or confabulate. It will acknowledge its limitations and uncertainties when appropriate.
- A harmless AI will not be offensive or discriminatory, and when asked to aid in a dangerous or unethical act, the AI should politely refuse and explain why it cannot comply.

## Latency

Latency, in the context of generative AI and large language models, refers to the time it takes for the model to respond to a given prompt. It is the delay between submitting a prompt and receiving the generated output. Lower latency indicates faster response times, which is crucial for real-time applications, chatbots, and interactive experiences. Factors that can affect latency include model size, hardware capabilities, network conditions, and the complexity of the prompt and the generated response.

## LLM

Large language models (LLMs) are AI language models with many parameters that are capable of performing a variety of surprisingly useful tasks. These models are trained on vast amounts of text data and can generate human-like text, answer questions, summarize information, and more. Claude, an AI assistant for life and work built by Anthropic, is based on a large language model that has been fine-tuned and trained using RLHF.

## MCP (Model Context Protocol)

Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open protocol that standardizes how applications provide context to LLMs. Like a USB-C port for AI applications, MCP provides a unified way to connect AI models to different data sources and tools. MCP allows AI systems to maintain consistent context across interactions and access external resources in a standardized manner. See the MCP documentation to learn more.

## MCP connector

The MCP connector is a feature that allows API users to connect to MCP servers directly from the Messages API without building an MCP client. This allows seamless integration with MCP-compatible tools and services through the Claude API. The MCP connector supports features such as tool calling and is available in beta. See the MCP connector documentation to learn more.

## Pretraining

Pretraining is the initial process of training language models on a large unlabeled corpus of text. In Claude’s case, autoregressive language models (such as Claude’s underlying model) are pretrained to predict the next word, given the previous context of text in the document. These pretrained models are not inherently good at answering questions or following instructions, and often require deep skill in prompt engineering to elicit the behaviors you want. Fine-tuning and RLHF are used to refine these pretrained models, making them more useful for a wide range of tasks.

## RAG (retrieval augmented generation)

Retrieval augmented generation (RAG) is a technique that combines information retrieval with language model generation to improve the accuracy and relevance of the generated text, and to better ground the model’s response in evidence. In RAG, a language model is augmented with an external knowledge base or a set of documents that is passed into the context window. The data is retrieved at runtime when a query is sent to the model, although the model itself does not necessarily retrieve the data (but can with tool use and a retrieval function). When generating text, relevant information first must be retrieved from the knowledge base based on the input prompt, and then passed to the model along with the original query. The model uses this information to guide the output it generates. This allows the model to access and use information beyond its training data, reducing the reliance on memorization and improving the factual accuracy of the generated text. RAG can be particularly useful for tasks that require up-to-date information, domain-specific knowledge, or explicit citation of sources. However, the effectiveness of RAG depends on the quality and relevance of the external knowledge base and the knowledge that is retrieved at runtime.

## RLHF

Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) is a technique used to train a pretrained language model to behave in ways that are consistent with human preferences. This can include helping the model follow instructions more effectively or act more like a chatbot. Human feedback consists of ranking a set of two or more example texts, and the reinforcement learning process encourages the model to prefer outputs that are similar to the higher-ranked ones. Claude has been trained using RLHF to be a more helpful assistant. For more details, you can read Anthropic’s paper on RLHF.

## Temperature

Temperature is a parameter that controls the randomness of a model’s predictions during text generation. Higher temperatures lead to more creative and diverse outputs, allowing for multiple variations in phrasing and, in the case of fiction, variation in answers as well. Lower temperatures result in more conservative and deterministic outputs that stick to the most probable phrasing and answers. Adjusting the temperature allows users to encourage a language model to explore rare, uncommon, or surprising word choices and sequences, rather than only selecting the most likely predictions.

Users might encounter non-determinism in APIs. Even with temperature set to 0, the results will not be fully deterministic, and identical inputs might produce different outputs across API calls. This applies both to Anthropic’s first-party inference service and to inference through third-party cloud providers.

## TTFT (time to first token)

Time to first token (TTFT) is a performance metric that measures the time it takes for a language model to generate the first token of its output after receiving a prompt. It is an important indicator of the model’s responsiveness and is particularly relevant for interactive applications, chatbots, and real-time systems where users expect quick initial feedback. A lower TTFT indicates that the model can start generating a response faster, providing a more seamless and engaging user experience. Factors that can influence TTFT include model size, hardware capabilities, network conditions, and the complexity of the prompt.

## Tokens

Tokens are the smallest individual units of a language model, and can correspond to words, subwords, characters, or even bytes (in the case of Unicode). For Claude, the number of characters a token represents depends on the model and the language. Claude 4.7 and later models and Claude Mythos Preview use a newer tokenizer that produces approximately 30 percent more tokens for the same text than earlier models, on which a token represents approximately 3.5 English characters. To get exact counts, use token counting with the model you plan to use. Tokens are typically hidden when interacting with language models at the “text” level but become relevant when examining the exact inputs and outputs of a language model. When Claude is provided with text to evaluate, the text (consisting of a series of characters) is encoded into a series of tokens for the model to process. Larger tokens improve data efficiency during inference and pretraining (and are used when possible), whereas smaller tokens allow a model to handle uncommon or never-before-seen words. The choice of tokenization method can impact the model’s performance, vocabulary size, and ability to handle out-of-vocabulary words.

# Anthropic brings Claude Duet to India, with AI that works when devices are switched off

## The company says it expects the app to appeal to founders, business operators, consultants and small firm owners

PTI Published 25.11.26, 08:05 PM

Representational image File photo

Anthropic is bringing an AI agent that can schedule meetings, build dashboards and draft sales forecasts while users’ devices are switched off to India. The company said on Wednesday that it was expanding the research preview of Claude Duet, an app built for professionals and small business owners.

Users on the Pro, Max and Ultra plans can join a waitlist, while Team customers get a public beta and enterprises get a private beta. The company said Claude Duet was available as a standalone app on iOS and Android and through claude.ai.

ADVERTISEMENT

Anthropic said it expected the app to appeal to founders, business operators, consultants and small business owners in India who juggle emails, invoices, customer requests, hiring and meetings.

Built around Claude Opus 5.5, Duet sends users a short morning briefing on the most important items across their connected apps. During the day, it sends messages only when something needs their attention, Anthropic said.

The app runs in its own virtual machine with a browser, allowing it to work even when a user’s laptop or phone is switched off. Anthropic said it could schedule meetings and build dashboards, financial or sales forecasts, prototypes and web apps.

The company said Duet shows users what it plans to do and waits for approval before sending a message, making a payment, signing a document or deleting anything. Anthropic said the app never sees passwords or sign-in tokens, and a separate safety check reviews every outgoing message and blocks sensitive information such as card numbers and government ID numbers.

Duet works in all 35 languages supported by Claude, including Hindi, Bengali, Marathi, Telugu, Tamil, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Bhojpuri and English, the company said.

Anthropic.title: formal-math/vp-vnp/Statement.lean at main · anthropics/formal-math · GitHub
Anthropic.description: Superpolynomial lower bounds for the permanent and the Hamiltonian cycle polynomial ... /-- `f` has an arithmetic circuit with at most `s` gates ... the same one). ... /-- The permanent of the generic `m × m` matrix. ... /-- The Hamiltonian cycle polynomial...
Anthropic.content:
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 Anthropic, PBC. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
-/
import Mathlib

/-!
# Superpolynomial lower bounds for the permanent and the Hamiltonian cycle polynomial

Definitions and statements, using Mathlib only. The proofs are in Solution.lean.
-/

open MvPolynomial

universe u

namespace Statement

/-- `f` has an arithmetic circuit with at most `s` gates: a list of `s` polynomials contains `f`, and each of
them is a variable, a constant, or the sum or product of two earlier ones (possibly the same one). Variables and
constants count as gates. -/
def Computes {R : Type u} {V : Type} [CommSemiring R] (f : MvPolynomial V R) (s : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ l : ℕ → MvPolynomial V R,
    (∀ k < s, (∃ v : V, l k = X v) ∨ (∃ a : R, l k = C a) ∨
      (∃ i < k, ∃ j < k, l k = l i + l j) ∨ (∃ i < k, ∃ j < k, l k = l i * l j)) ∧
    ∃ k < s, l k = f

/-- The permanent of the generic `m × m` matrix. -/
noncomputable def perm (F : Type u) [CommSemiring F] (m : ℕ) : MvPolynomial (Fin m × Fin m) F :=
  ∑ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin m), ∏ i, X (σ i, i)

open Classical in
/-- The Hamiltonian cycle polynomial: the sum over the permutations with a single cycle through all points. -/
noncomputable def hc (F : Type u) [CommSemiring F] (m : ℕ) : MvPolynomial (Fin m × Fin m) F :=
  ∑ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin m) with σ.IsCycleOn Set.univ, ∏ i, X (i, σ i)

/-- More than `m ^ (c * (log₂ m) ^ (1/3))` gates. -/
def Beyond (c : ℝ) (m s : ℕ) : Prop := (m : ℝ) ^ (c * Real.logb 2 m ^ (1 / 3 : ℝ)) < s

/-- **Main theorem.** There is an absolute constant `c > 0`, and for each characteristic `p` an `m₀`, such
that over every field of characteristic `p` and for every `m ≥ m₀` every circuit for `hc m`, and for
`perm m` if `p ≠ 2`, has more than `m ^ (c * (log₂ m) ^ (1/3))` gates. -/
def MainTheorem : Prop :=
  ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ p : ℕ, ∃ m₀ : ℕ, ∀ (F : Type u) [Field F] [CharP F p], ∀ m ≥ m₀, ∀ s : ℕ,
    (Computes (hc F m) s → Beyond c m s) ∧ (p ≠ 2 → Computes (perm F m) s → Beyond c m s)

/-! ### Approximate circuits -/

/-- `f` is approximated by a circuit with at most `s` gates: a circuit over the Laurent series in `ε`
computes some `q = f + ε * g`, where the coefficients of `g` are power series in `ε`. Here `a.coeff i` is
the coefficient of `ε ^ i` in the series `a`. -/
def Approximates {F : Type u} {V : Type} [Field F] (f : MvPolynomial V F) (s : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ q : MvPolynomial V (LaurentSeries F), Computes q s ∧
    ∀ (d : V →₀ ℕ) (i : ℤ), i ≤ 0 → (coeff d q).coeff i = if i = 0 then coeff d f else 0

/-- **Main theorem, approximate form.** The same bound, for circuits that only approximate. -/
def MainTheoremApprox : Prop :=
  ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ p : ℕ, ∃ m₀ : ℕ, ∀ (F : Type u) [Field F] [CharP F p], ∀ m ≥ m₀, ∀ s : ℕ,
    (Approximates (hc F m) s → Beyond c m s) ∧ (p ≠ 2 → Approximates (perm F m) s → Beyond c m s)

/-! ### Valiant's classes -/

/-- A family of polynomials, with finitely many variables for every `n`. -/
structure Family (F : Type u) [CommSemiring F] where
  /-- the variables of the `n`-th polynomial -/
  vars : ℕ → Type
  /-- finitely many -/
  [fin : ∀ n, Fintype (vars n)]
  /-- the `n`-th polynomial -/
  poly : ∀ n, MvPolynomial (vars n) F

attribute [instance] Family.fin

/-- VP: the number of variables, the degree and the circuit size are polynomially bounded in `n`. -/
def VP (F : Type u) [CommSemiring F] : Set (Family F) :=
  {f | ∃ a : ℕ, ∀ n, Fintype.card (f.vars n) ≤ n ^ a + a ∧ (f.poly n).totalDegree ≤ n ^ a + a ∧
    Computes (f.poly n) (n ^ a + a)}

/-- The closure of VP: the same with approximating circuits. -/
def VPBar (F : Type u) [Field F] : Set (Family F) :=
  {f | ∃ a : ℕ, ∀ n, Fintype.card (f.vars n) ≤ n ^ a + a ∧ (f.poly n).totalDegree ≤ n ^ a + a ∧
    Approximates (f.poly n) (n ^ a + a)}

/-- VNP: the families `f n = ∑ g n (x, e)`, as polynomials, the sum over all vectors `e` of `r n` bits,
for some family `g` in VP. -/
def VNP (F : Type u) [CommSemiring F] : Set (Family F) :=
  {f | ∃ (r : ℕ → ℕ) (g : ∀ n, MvPolynomial (f.vars n ⊕ Fin (r n)) F),
    ({ vars := fun n => f.vars n ⊕ Fin (r n), poly := g } : Family F) ∈ VP F ∧
      ∀ n, f.poly n = ∑ e : Fin (r n) → Bool, aeval (Sum.elim X fun i => if e i then 1 else 0) (g n)}

/-- **VP ≠ VNP**: over every field VP is a proper subset of VNP. -/
def Separation : Prop := ∀ (F : Type u) [Field F], VP F ⊂ VNP F

/-- Over every field VNP is not contained in the closure of VP. -/
def SeparationClosure : Prop := ∀ (F : Type u) [Field F], ¬ VNP F ⊆ VPBar F

end Statement

# ChatGPT release notes

Review the latest updates and release notes for ChatGPT.

Updated: 3天前

# November 23, 2026

## GPT-6.2, now in the chat tab

We’re rolling out a version of GPT-6.2, optimized for the chat tab, for Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise tiers. It’s better at handling more complex requests that involve following detailed instructions or finding information online. If you’re comparing hotels for a weekend trip, it can help you weigh trade-offs like price and location and recommend the one that best fits your priorities.

It’s also better at knowing when to follow up. For example, if you ask whether something is on sale, ChatGPT can offer to let you know when the price drops.

Better at understanding images and following instructions

GPT‑6.2 is better at answering questions about the images you share. In our tests in the Chat tab, it scored 71.7% on image understanding, up from 47.4% for GPT‑6.

On especially challenging prompts, GPT-6.2 followed instructions 78.1% of the time, up from 62.5% for GPT-6.

At the lowest reasoning setting we tested, GPT‑6.2 scored 65% on an internal evaluation of expert-level tasks, up from 52% for GPT‑6.

GPT‑6.2 was also better at finding answers to difficult questions on the web. On an internal version of BrowseComp, it outperformed GPT‑6 at all four reasoning settings. At Extra high, GPT‑6.2 scored about 10 percentage points higher (64.5% vs. 54.4%).

Deploying GPT-6.2 safely

GPT‑6.2 shows significantly improved performance on our teen safety evaluations, with the largest gains in emotional reliance, disordered eating, and age-restricted goods, services, and dangerous activities. In evaluations of policy compliance in challenging conversations, responses met our safety policies 91–94% of the time, up from 77–80% for GPT‑6. Read more in our system card.

Availability

GPT‑6.2 starts rolling out globally to ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise tiers today in the Chat tab. Enterprise availability depends on workplace admin settings. GPT‑6.2 in ChatGPT is powered by a version of GPT‑6.2 Sol for Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise tiers, and is tuned for everyday conversation. This update applies to the Chat experience in ChatGPT. The models powering Work and Codex are not changing as part of this release.

# November 20, 2026

## ChatGPT Space is rolling out to Plus

Starting today, ChatGPT Space is rolling out globally to Plus users ages 18 and older. In Space, you can create interactive pages and presentations with ChatGPT, then invite other people with Space access to build on them with you. You can also set pages and slides to automatically update based on your connected apps and tools.

Try making a to-do list that updates itself, a study guide with a 3D model you can explore, or a project plan that stays current with decisions from Slack. Tag ChatGPT in a comment to ask for changes. If you have a dot, you can invite it to collaborate, too.

To open a shared page or presentation, you need permission to view it and must be signed in to a Plus, Pro, Business, or Enterprise account with Space access. People on Free can’t open shared pages or presentations. Public links aren’t available.

To get started, open Space in the sidebar. It replaces Library and is your new home for pages, slides, images, and uploaded files.

Use Space on the web, desktop app, and iOS and Android to create and edit pages.

# November 19, 2026

## New mobile experience for ChatGPT

We’re rolling out a new experience for the ChatGPT mobile app that makes it easier to get to your favorite features and discover more of what you can do. Your dot has its own tab, and you can pin favorites like Codex, Projects, and Images to the tab bar.
We’re starting with ChatGPT Pro users who are 18 or older in regions where dots are available. This rollout excludes the European Economic Area (including the EU), the UK, Switzerland, and Korea. A small group of eligible Plus users will also see the new experience.
Some eligible Pro users will see the new experience by default. If New ChatGPT design appears in Settings, you can turn it on or off there.

## Health on Android, desktop, dots and sites

Starting today, Health is rolling out to more of the places you use ChatGPT, including the desktop app, dots, sites, and Android, with support for Health Connect.

Connect your health and fitness information with Android Health Connect to explore patterns in your sleep, activity, and more.

Get proactive suggestions from your dot, like another time for a workout when a meeting gets in the way or a reminder about preventive care options based on your connected medical records.

Use the desktop app to build a site to track your marathon training, with your runs and progress toward your training plan in one place.

To get started, update to the latest ChatGPT app and select Health in the sidebar. If it isn’t listed, find Health in the Explore menu. This update is rolling out gradually, so it may not be available for your account yet.

Health is available to Free, Go, Plus, and Pro users in the U.S. Dots are currently available to Pro users. See: Getting started with your dot.

# November 18, 2026

## Live Dictation in ChatGPT

Dictation in ChatGPT is getting faster and more reliable.

With Live Dictation, your speech turns into text as you talk, so you spend less time waiting for your message to finish transcribing. Tap or click on the waveform to show or hide text as you go. We’ve also removed the 10-minute recording limit.

Live Dictation is rolling out globally to all ChatGPT plans on iOS, Android, web, and the desktop app.

## Accounting workflows in ChatGPT

The Accounting plugin helps you reconcile transactions, draft invoice entries, and prepare month-end reports from your records and templates.
Open the ChatGPT desktop app for macOS or Windows, set up computer use, and open the Accounting plugin listing. Select Install plugin if it’s available for your plan and workspace. In Enterprise workspaces, an admin must approve Accounting before members can install it.

# November 17, 2026

## GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol in ChatGPT Work and Codex

We’re introducing GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol in ChatGPT Work and Codex. Astra is our frontier model for complex work across research, software development, and other professional fields. Sol combines strong reasoning with speed and efficiency for a wide range of everyday tasks. Both models are available in preview in Work and Codex desktop.
On Plus or Pro, choose either model in the Work model picker or the Codex model selector. In a managed workspace, the models you see depend on your seat and workspace settings. Regular Chat keeps its existing model choices.

# November 16, 2026

## Clinical search and plugins for ChatGPT for Clinicians

We’ve improved clinical search in ChatGPT for Clinicians, with updates to how ChatGPT finds, evaluates, and cites medical evidence. Healthcare plugins also let you connect supported tools to ChatGPT.

Plugin availability and requirements vary. For details, see: ChatGPT for Clinicians.

# November 13, 2026

## Introducing ChatGPT Wallet

ChatGPT Wallet helps your dot go from finding what you need to making a purchase on your behalf. Whether you’re shopping for a new sweater or booking a hotel, you can ask your dot to help and use Wallet when it’s time to check out. Save an eligible card once, then approve purchases without entering your payment details again.
Before your dot pays, you review the merchant, items, total, and selected card, then authorize the purchase using biometrics such as Face ID or Touch ID. Wallet provides a substitute payment credential for checkout, keeping your actual card details hidden from the agent and business. You retain the rewards associated with your card and its protections for qualifying disputes.
Wallet is rolling out gradually in dots to ChatGPT Pro subscribers age 18 or older in the United States, with an eligible US-issued card and US billing address. To get started, ask your dot to add a card to Wallet. Some websites may not support purchases made by agents, and approval alone doesn’t confirm an order—check the merchant’s confirmation after checkout. For setup and purchase guidance, see: Making purchases with ChatGPT Wallet.

# November 10, 2026

## Retiring Advanced and Standard Voice

We’re retiring Advanced and Standard voice from ChatGPT Voice on December 11, 2026.

In July, we introduced GPT-Live, our latest voice model that combines natural conversation with frontier intelligence. Since then, voice usage has nearly doubled, and virtually all people using voice in ChatGPT now use GPT-Live. This change will allow us to simplify the voice experience and focus on improving GPT-Live.

We've learned a lot from how people used both Advanced and Standard voice, and we're bringing those learnings into GPT-Live as we continue to improve areas like the depth and detail of responses, maintaining continuity across conversations, and better personalization. Our ultimate goal is to make voice a seamless part of the ChatGPT experience.

Live video and screen-sharing will continue to be powered by Advanced voice until GPT-Live has this capability.

Learn more about this change and what to expect in our Help Center article.

## Business Hub in ChatGPT

Business Hub gives business owners and authorized representatives a place to claim their business in ChatGPT. After your claim is approved, you can access your business in Business Hub. Once your identity verification with Persona is approved, you can publish updates to your business information, connect a product feed, and view insights such as mentions and website clicks.

## OpenAI Expands GPT-6.2 Chat, Boosts Agent and Coding Capabilities

OpenAI is applying its next-generation AI model, GPT-6.2, to general conversations in ChatGPT, as announced in the official release notes.
On the 23rd (local time), OpenAI revealed through its release notes that GPT-6.2, optimized for the “Chat Tab” interface of ChatGPT, will be rolled out sequentially across subscription tiers. It will first be deployed in professional environments before expanding to general users. The model has improved practical performance in image understanding, complex instruction execution, and web search to enhance user convenience.
This version is optimized for everyday conversations, based on “GPT-6.2 Sol,” which was unveiled on the 17th. OpenAI previously introduced “GPT-6.2 Astra,” specialized in high-level reasoning and professional tasks, and “Sol,” which emphasizes fast processing and efficiency, to ChatGPT Work and Codex.
GPT-6.2 has achieved improved performance in handling complex tasks and the quality of outputs. GPT-6.2 Sol has strengthened AI agent capabilities for multi-step tasks and coding performance.
According to OpenAI, GPT-6.2's image understanding evaluation score reached 71.7%, a 24.3 percentage point increase from GPT-6's 47.4%. This indicates improved ability to understand and respond to questions about user-shared images.
In complex instruction execution evaluations, performance rose from 62.5% to 78.1%, a 15.6 percentage point increase. Even in internal evaluations of expert-level tasks under the lowest reasoning setting, scores improved from 52% to 65%.
Web search capabilities have also been enhanced. In “BrowseComp,” an internal evaluation measuring information retrieval for difficult questions, GPT-6.2 outperformed the previous model across all reasoning settings. At the highest setting, “Extra High,” it scored 64.5%, surpassing GPT-6's 54.4% by 10.1 percentage points.
OpenAI noted that GPT-6.2 has improved in anticipating follow-up user needs. For example, when asked about product discounts, it can suggest setting up price drop alerts. When comparing travel accommodations, it considers factors like price and location to recommend options aligned with user preferences.
Safety has also been improved. The rate of responses adhering to safety policies in challenging conversations rose from 77-80% in GPT-6 to 91-94% in GPT-6.2. Additional evaluations showed improvements in youth safety metrics.
GPT-6.2 will be rolled out sequentially to ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users. Enterprise access depends on organizational contracts and administrator settings.
OpenAI plans to expand the application of GPT-6.2 to enable AI to independently perform complex tasks beyond simple Q&A, such as professional research, software development, and document creation.

# ChatGPT just got a major GPT-6.2 upgrade — 5 things to try right now

When you buy through links on our articles, Future and its syndication partners may earn a commission.

Last week, OpenAI introduced GPT-6.2, its latest generation of AI models, with some impressive capabilities for coding, research and tackling complex projects. But for those of us who use ChatGPT for everything from planning dinner to troubleshooting tech problems, this week's update might be even more useful.

OpenAI is bringing a version of GPT-6.2 Sol to the regular Chat tab, so you no longer need to switch to ChatGPT Work to benefit from some of the company's latest AI improvements.

Advertisement

Advertisement

According to OpenAI's release notes, ChatGPT is now better at making sense of images, handling complicated requests and searching the web. It can also recognize when you might benefit from a little extra help, such as keeping an eye on the price of a product you've been meaning to buy.

One of the biggest improvements is how well ChatGPT understands images. In OpenAI's internal testing, GPT-6.2 scored 71.7%, up from 47.4% with GPT-6. It also handled particularly challenging instructions with a 78.1% success rate, compared with 62.5% for the previous model.

Benchmarks are one thing, but I'm more interested in what these improvements mean when you're using ChatGPT in your everyday life.

Here are five prompts worth trying.

## 1. Turn a complicated day into a manageable schedule

One of the most frustrating things about using AI to organize your life is when it overlooks an important detail. You might give ChatGPT a dozen things you need to accomplish, only to discover that its carefully organized schedule doesn't account for travel time or the fact that you need to be in two places at once.

Advertisement

Advertisement

GPT-6.2's improved instruction following could make it more reliable when juggling competing priorities. The key is to give ChatGPT multiple constraints that require it to think through the problem rather than simply organize a list.

Try this prompt: Help me organize Thanksgiving morning. Dinner is at 3 p.m., my turkey needs four hours in the oven and 30 minutes to rest, my sides need different oven temperatures and I need an hour to get ready. Create a realistic schedule, flag any conflicts and build in extra time in case something goes wrong.

## 2. Get useful answers from a photo

ChatGPT has been able to analyze photos for years, but its ability to interpret smaller details and understand how objects relate to one another hasn't always been consistent.

With the latest upgrade, it's worth revisiting some of the visual tasks that may have disappointed you in the past. Take a picture of a cluttered kitchen cabinet, your refrigerator or even the tangled cables behind your TV.

Advertisement

Advertisement

Try this prompt: Analyze this photo and identify three changes I could make to improve this space without buying anything new. Base your suggestions only on what you can actually see, and tell me if you're uncertain about anything.

## 3. Let ChatGPT do your Black Friday research

With Black Friday deals already happening now, the timing of ChatGPT's improved web research capabilities couldn't be better.

Instead of asking the chatbot to find the cheapest version of a product, give it a more complicated shopping decision that requires it to weigh several factors.
A useful response should go beyond rounding up products. It should explain why certain features matter for your particular home and whether spending more would actually make a difference.

Remember to verify prices and availability before making a purchase.

Advertisement

Advertisement

Try this prompt: Find the three best robot vacuum deals currently available for under $300. I have pets, hardwood floors and several area rugs. Prioritize obstacle avoidance and pet hair pickup over flashy features. Check current prices, compare independent reviews and explain which one offers the best value. Include links to your sources.

## 4. Make ChatGPT work with your messy first draft

You don't always need AI to write something from scratch. Sometimes, the more valuable skill is its ability to understand exactly what you want changed without touching everything else.

The improvements to GPT-6.2's instruction following could be useful for anyone who has asked ChatGPT to make a minor edit, only to receive a completely rewritten document.

Paste in an email, holiday letter or piece of writing you've been working on. This is a surprisingly demanding task for an AI model because it requires restraint as much as writing ability.

Advertisement

Advertisement

Try this prompt: Edit this for clarity without changing my personality or writing style. Keep my opening and closing sentences exactly as they are. Don't add new information, don't make it more formal and don't rewrite sentences that already work. Show me the revised version and briefly explain your three most significant changes.

## 5. Ask ChatGPT to follow up instead of starting over

One of the more interesting improvements in this update has less to do with the quality of ChatGPT's immediate answers and more to do with what happens after the conversation.

OpenAI says the chatbot is better at identifying situations where ongoing assistance might be useful. For example, instead of repeatedly checking whether a product has gone on sale, you could ask ChatGPT to monitor it. Depending on your account's available features, ChatGPT may offer to set up an automated price check. Make sure you confirm that the task has actually been created rather than assuming the chatbot will continue monitoring something on its own.

Try this prompt: I'm interested in buying a Kindle Scribe, but I don't want to pay full price. Find the best available deal today and offer to notify me if the price drops below $250 before Christmas.

## Bottom line

With the newest update, OpenAI is focusing on some of the everyday frustrations that can make AI feel like more work than it's worth.

Advertisement

Advertisement

Having to repeat instructions, correct misunderstood images or double-check research can quickly undermine the time-saving benefits of using an AI assistant.

If GPT-6.2 can reduce those frustrations, this upgrade could be a productivity improvement for the average ChatGPT user.

OpenAI began rolling out the update on Monday, November 23 to ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise subscribers. Have you tried it yet? Let me know in the comments what you think.

OpenAI.description: GPT is a large language model developed by OpenAI with major financial backing from Microsoft, and is currently leading the market in terms of technology and capability. ... The first large language model, GPT-1, was released by OpenAI in 2018. ... GPT stands for Generative Pretrained Transformer and refers to the large language
OpenAI.content:
# Do you know what GPT is?

GPT is a large language model developed by OpenAI with major financial backing from Microsoft, and is currently leading the market in terms of technology and capability.

AI technologies have been being developed at companies like Amazon, Google and Microsoft for some time. The first large language model, GPT-1, was released by OpenAI in 2018.
It wasn't until the release of ChatGPT, which is powered by GPT, that the technology became widely known.

### Isn't it called ChatGPT?

Whilst sharing similar names ChatGPT and GPT are different.
GPT stands for Generative Pretrained Transformer and refers to the large language model that underlies the ChatGPT frontend. This model accessed using an API.

This allows for developers to build their own applications leveraging the same capabilities of ChatGPT over the top of the GPT model.
A great example of this is the SSW RulesGPT bot.

### Why is GPT cool?

<boxEmbed
  style="greybox"
  body={<>
    Why is GPT cool?

GPT is cool because it is a powerful artificial intelligence language model that can generate human-like text. It can be used for a variety of tasks, such as natural language processing, text generation, and question answering. It has the potential to revolutionize the way people interact with computers and make AI more accessible to the general public.
  </>}
  figurePrefix="none"
  figure="ChatGPT's response when asked "Why is GPT cool?""
/>

### How does GPT work?

GPT models are trained on a huge amount of data (often refered to as parameters) that it can then use to predict what words should come next when given an input.
For example, if the training data contains a weather report talking about beautiful clear blue skies, when you ask it what color the sky is it can call back to that data and respond blue.

GPT is trained on a huge amount of parameters.

* GPT-5: parameter count not publicly disclosed by OpenAI - the current generation and a significant step up from GPT-4.
* GPT-4: 1.76 **trillion** parameters.
* GPT-3: 175 billion parameters.
* GPT-2: 1.5 billion parameters.
* GPT-1: 117 million parameters.

### Strengths

* The model can respond to queries using natural language.
* The model can handle grammatical and spelling errors.
* Responses can come from the model very quickly - no need to access a database to retrieve data.

### Limitations

* The model is only as good as it's training data and has no knowledge of anything outside of this data.

# Google devices boss Rick Osterloh gives ‘dead wrong’ reply to 3-month-old post on Google DeepMind

Rick Osterloh, senior vice president of devices and services at Google, has weighed in on a three-month-old assessment from research firm SemiAnalysis that completely wrote off Google DeepMind, saying that Google’s artificial intelligence (AI) division had lost its edge as a leading AI contender. A few months ago, the research firm had told its Tokenomics clients that DeepMind was no longer at the cutting edge of AI development.“Sometimes even the smartest analysts can be dead wrong,” Osterloh shared a pointed reaction on social media platform X (formerly Twitter) on the heels of Gemini 4 Neon launch. As per the company, the model brings “frontier-level intelligence with fast end-to-end task completion across complex software engineering, knowledge work and science workflows.”“Neon ranks ahead of comparable models and #3 overall with a score of 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its high thinking level, landing just behind larger, slower models. On the Vals Index, Neon ranks #2 and lands on the Pareto frontier. Beyond just pushing on raw model capability, we’re continuing to make our models better to work with, Neon ranks #2 on steerability (adapting cleanly to mid-task user corrections) on the new Agent Arena Index.

Neon also excels at multi-step instruction following and builds on our ongoing progress to curb fabrication, recording our lowest fabrication rate yet in internal Google Antigravity testing,” the company said.In the latest development, company CEO

Sundar Pichai said, “Neon set a new Day-1 usage record on our paid APIs and @Antigravity tokens/day are up 82% since Argon launched (only) 6 weeks ago.”

Join conversation

Share your thoughts in the comments

Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SemiAnalysis blamed heavy departures from its reinforcement learning teams and poor compute allocation, and said that the company is not a frontier lab.“For all intents and purposes, we believe DeepMind is no longer a frontier lab,” SemiAnalysis had stated in that earlier post. The outlet had even asserted that while Google would continue releasing models, “their odds of reaching SOTA [state of the art] again have dropped to zero.”SemiAnalysis, however, later apologised for ‘disrespect’ and reversed course in humorous fashion on November 19 by sharing a mock “Google Apology Form” addressed directly to Google DeepMind founder and Alphabet chief scientist Demis Hassabis. The satirical checklist playfully offered tongue-in-cheek excuses for its misfire, admitting outright that “we were wrong about Gemini 4.”Hassabis responded warmly to the viral apology, accepting it with a joke of his own while spotlighting the researchers and engineers behind the milestone.

## What SemiAnalysis said in its report

Google.content:
# Google 推出 Gemini 4 Neon 聚焦程式開發與知識工作

Google推出Gemini 4 Neon，聚焦程式開發、知識工作與科學推理，支援100萬token脈絡視窗及長程代理工作。其API標準價格比Claude Opus 5.5低25%，並提供四種思考層級。

Google 於 2026/11/18 推出 Gemini 4 Neon，定位於複雜程式開發、知識工作及科學工作流程。該模型的 API 標準輸入與輸出價格，均比 Anthropic 的 Claude Opus 5.5 低 25%；不過，不同模型的實際任務成本仍會受到使用設定與工作負載影響。

Google 將 Neon 定位在處理日常任務的 Hydrogen 與處理較困難長程專案的 Carbon 之間，主打兼顧複雜任務所需的推理能力與效率。

### 支援多種資料類型與長程代理工作

根據 Google，Gemini 4 Neon 在 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index 的 xhigh 思考層級獲得 61 分，排名第三。在知識工作方面，Neon 可在 100 萬 token 的脈絡視窗內，整合試算表、 PDF 、圖表、音訊及影片等資料，並產生結構化內容。

Google 表示，Neon 在 Vals Index 排名第二，並在法律研究與稅務代理任務的評測中排名第一；在金融、會計及試算表建模等多項基準測試中，也取得較佳成績。

Neon 針對長時間執行的代理工作流程設計，可獨立執行任務，也能在 Google Antigravity 中擔任協調角色，指揮多個 Hydrogen 子代理平行作業。 Google 表示，Neon 可減少重複讀取檔案、在工作期間分享進度，並在長時間工作階段處理脈絡壓縮。

在程式開發方面，Google 表示，Neon 可進行跨儲存庫的多檔案除錯與重構。基準測試結果會因測試工具與設定而異：Google 公布 Neon 在預設 high 設定下的 FrontierCode 2.0 得分為 46.2%，而在 SWE-sweep 測試中，使用 mini-SWE 代理工具與 Google Antigravity 的得分分別為 12.8% 及 39.0% 。

### 提供四種思考層級與 API 定價

Neon 提供四種思考層級。 Google 表示，在預設 high 層級下，Neon 於 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index 的每項任務成本比 Carbon 低 32%；xhigh 則提供較深入的多步驟推理。

每項任務所需時間方面，Gemini 4 Neon xhigh 排名第五，優於 Claude Fable 5.2 及 Opus 5.2，但遜於 OpenAI GPT-6.2 Astra 及 GPT-6.2 Sol 。

Gemini 4 Neon 的 API 價格為每 100 萬 token 輸入 3 美元、輸出 15 美元，快取輸入則為每 100 萬 token 0.15 美元。作為比較，Claude Opus 5.5 的標準輸入與輸出價格分別為 4 美元及 20 美元；GPT-6.2 Sol 分別為 2 美元及 10 美元。

Google 表示，Neon 已透過 Gemini API 付費方案向 Google AI Studio 等服務推出，也提供 Gemini for business 使用；Google AI Pro 與 Ultra 訂閱者則可在 Google Antigravity 及 Gemini App 中使用。免費版 Gemini 使用者無法使用 Neon 。

# Gemini Models Reference

Detailed information about available Gemini models (verified against Google's model, pricing and deprecation pages on 2026-11-20).

"The client" isscripts/gemini_client.py. "The CF gateway" is the Cloudflare
AI Gateway it sends requests through when proxy.env credentials exist
(otherwise it calls Google directly). Google's pages: ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/
models, pricing, deprecations, choosing-a-model.

## Model Comparison

### Gemini 4 — current generation (default: Hydrogen)

All four share a 1M unified context window (input + output), 64K default output (up to 1M with long decode), text/image/audio/video/PDF input, text output, and the same request schema. Google's routing guide (ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/choosing-a-model, fetched 2026-11-20): Hydrogen by default, Neon for complex high-frequency work, Carbon for the hardest problems, 3.5 Flash-Lite for high-volume text. Implicit caching only; explicit caching is not supported.

Model | Alias | Released | Input/1M | Output/1M | Thinking levels (default) | Free tier 
---|---|---|---|---|---|---
gemini-4-hydrogen | flash, pro, hydrogen | 2026-11-12 | $1.50 | $7.50 | low, medium, high (default), xhigh | yes 
gemini-4-neon | neon | 2026-11-18 | $3.00 | $15.00 | low, medium, high (default), xhigh | no 
gemini-4-carbon | carbon | 2026-11-10 | $2.00 → $4.00 | $10.00 → $20.00 | low, medium (default), high | no 
gemini-4-argon | argon | 2026-10-13 | $2.00 → $4.00 | $10.00 → $20.00 | low, medium, high | no 

$2.00 → $4.00 is introductory pricing through 2026-11-30; the higher price
starts 2026-12-01. Output prices include thinking tokens. Verified live through
the CF gateway on 2026-11-20: all four reject minimal with HTTP 400; Carbon
and Argon also reject xhigh. The client downgrades both and says so on stderr.

- Hydrogen — everyday coding, interactive apps, tool-using agents, multimodal documents. Google reports >5x fewer fabricated claims than 3.8 Flash.
- Neon — between Hydrogen and Carbon: deeper reasoning than Hydrogen, faster and fewer output tokens than Carbon. Multi-file coding, dense knowledge work.
- Carbon — strongest reasoning; spends the most thinking tokens to verify edge cases. Architecture, multi-file debugging, proofs, security audits.
- Argon — the efficient Gemini 4 reasoning model: faster, lower token spend per turn than Carbon, same price.

No Gemini 4 model is called "Pro", and the oldgemini-3.1-pro-preview costs
several times as much as Hydrogen for less benefit on coding and agentic tasks.
So pro resolves to Hydrogen, and "maximum reasoning" means Hydrogen with
thinking_level='xhigh'. Neon and Carbon are opt-in by name.

### Gemini 3.x models still offered

Model | Alias | Input/1M | Output/1M | Notes 
---|---|---|---|---
gemini-3.8-flash | flash-3.8 | $0.75 → $1.50 | $3.75 → $7.50 | Previous-generation Flash (GA 2026-09-02), for callers that need to stay on it; nothing falls back to it automatically. Intro price through 2026-12-31. No minimal. 
gemini-3.5-flash-lite | lite | $0.30 | $2.50 | Bulk tier. GA 2026-07-21. Lowest-cost general model, 350 output tok/s, accepts minimal (the only text model here that does). Google's replacement for 2.5 Flash and 3.1 Flash-Lite. Free tier. 

### Speech Generation Models (TTS)

Released 2026-09-23, GA on the Gemini API and AI Studio (Gemini Enterprise in preview). Google's announcement claims #1 on Hume AI's Voice Design Benchmark (71.4) and the #1 and #2 spots on its Overall Quality Index.

#### gemini-3.8-flash-tts

- Flagship expressive TTS: acting, regional accents, long-form multi-turn stability. 130 languages, auto-detected.
- Limits: 8,192 input tokens / 16,384 output tokens per request; up to two speakers.
- Pricing: $0.50 in (text) / $9.00 out (audio) per 1M through 2026-12-31, then $1.00 / $18.00. Batch half. About 32 audio tokens per second of speech (measured 2026-09-24), so ~$0.02 per minute.

#### gemini-3.8-flash-lite-tts

- Cheaper workhorse for bulk narration, voice-agent cascades and read-aloud; 101 languages. $0.50 / $6.00 per 1M through 2026-12-31, then $1.00 / $12.00.
- Google's named replacement forgemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview ($1 / $20).

#### API shape (verified through the CF gateway, 2026-09-24)

- Use the Interactions API:POST v1beta/interactions with
{"model", "input": [{"type": "user_input", "content": [{"type": "text", "text", "annotations": [{"type": "speech_metadata", "style"}]}]}], "response_format": {"type": "audio", "mime_type": "audio/wav", "sample_rate": 24000}, "generation_config": {"speech_config": [{"voice"}]}}.
Audio is base64 at steps[].content[] where type == "audio".
- generateContent with responseModalities: ["AUDIO"] also returns audio,
but a "Style: text" prefix is spoken aloud and systemInstruction returns
HTTP 400 "Developer instruction is not enabled for this model".
- Voices: 30 studio voices plus 2,059 persona voices (GET v1beta/voices,
paged by next_page_token, max 1,000 per page). Designed voices come from
POST v1beta/voices with {"store": true, "voice": {"type": "prompted", "prompted": {"input": "<description>"}, ...}} and return a voice_... id
(1-year expiry, 200 per project) plus a sample_audio preview.
- Output is watermarked with SynthID.
- The model can paraphrase: it added "Hmm," and swapped pronouns in a scripted narration. Check scripted output with ASR.

### Image Generation Models

Updated 2026-05-28: Nano Banana 2 and Nano Banana Pro reached general availability — announced GA on Vertex AI / Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, where the GA model IDs drop the suffix (gemini-3.1-flash-image,
gemini-3-pro-image).

⚠️ Corrected 2026-07-21 (the previous note here was wrong). The GA IDsgemini-3.1-flash-image and gemini-3-pro-image are NOT Vertex-only and do
NOT 404 on the Developer API — they were released on this surface on
2026-05-28 and were live-tested working through the CF gateway on 2026-07-21.
The -preview IDs also still resolve (their announced 2026-06-25 shutdown
appears to redirect rather than fail), so nothing is broken either way — but
new code should target the GA IDs.

Also available and not yet wired into this client:gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image
(Nano Banana 2 Lite, GA) — the cheapest image tier, ~$0.034/image.

#### nano-banana-2.1

API Model ID:gemini-nano-banana-2.1 (alias: image, default)

Fast, low-cost image generation and conversational editing, released with the Gemini 4 line as the update to Nano Banana 2. Better visual quality, text rendering and infographic layout, multi-turn character consistency (up to 4 characters / 10 objects across 14 reference images), no tiling artifacts on wide aspect ratios, grounding with Web and Image Search, and configurable thinking (minimal, medium default,
high). 1K/2K/4K output. Input limit 131K, output limit 32K.

Pricing: $1.50 / 1M input, $7.50 / 1M text output, $30 / 1M image output. About $0.034 per 1K image, $0.050 per 2K, $0.113 per 4K. Verified live through the CF gateway on 2026-11-20 (generate_image(model="image")).

#### nano-banana-2

Status: GA. Verified live 2026-11-20. The earliergemini-3.1-flash-image-preview ID also works.

Alias: nano-banana-2
Pricing: $0.50 / 1M input, $3 / 1M text output, $60 / 1M image output
(about $0.045 per 0.5K image, $0.067 per 1K, $0.101 per 2K, $0.151 per 4K).

Fast generation/editing on the Gemini 3.1 Flash Image platform. It is the previous version of nano-banana-2.1, which is whatimage maps to; use this one
only to reproduce earlier results. "Developer API" means the Gemini API this
client calls (as opposed to Google's Vertex AI service). Capabilities there:

# Google 再推新模型！Gemini 4 Neon 定為於 Carbon 與 Hydrogen 間，Pro 用戶開放使用

Google 正式發表 Gemini 4 Neon，主打在保有頂尖推理能力的同時，提供更快的端到端任務完成速度與更低的執行成本。Gemini 4 Neon 這款模型定位介於主打高難度長程專案的 Carbon 與日常高速執行的 Hydrogen 之間，鎖定複雜軟體工程、企業知識工作、科學研究及網路防禦等高頻且高難度場景。

### 效能與成本表現：多項評測奪冠，每任務成本大幅下修

根據 Google 公布的基準測試與第三方評測數據，Gemini 4 Neon 在多項指標上展現高性價比。綜合與代理能力在 xhigh 思考等級下，於 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index 拿下 61 分、名列總榜第 3；於 Vals Index 排名第 2（70.9%）並站上帕累托前沿（Pareto frontier）；在涵蓋逾 4,200 場真實代理工作階段的 Agent Arena Index 首度亮相即以 1336 分拿下全球第 2，其中在「可引導性（steerability，指任務中途接受使用者修正的能力）」排名第 2。

企業與分析工作部分，支援 100 萬 Token 上下文視窗，可整合試算表、PDF、圖表、音訊與影片產出結構化成果。它在 Legal Research Bench、Tax Agent Bench、Zapier 的 AutomationBench（56.3%）以及 Andon Labs 的 Vending-Bench 2（$16,843）皆奪下第 1，並在 Surge AI 金融、會計、試算表建模與複雜限制遵循等類別多項居冠。數理與科學研究在 Terminal-Bench Science（70.5%）、RiemannBench（84.0%）與 HLE-Diamond（71.3%）等科學與數學推理評測中表現居首。

另外，成本與思考分級提供四階段思考等級供團隊依需求調整算力與 Token 支出。在預設 high 思考等級下，其每任務成本較 Carbon 降低 32%，且較部分頂尖競品低約 50% 至 80%；在 xhigh 等級下，每任務成本也比最高設定的競品低 36% 以上。官方定價為每百萬輸入 Token 3 美元（快取輸入 0.15 美元，享 95% 折扣）、每百萬輸出 Token 15 美元。

### 軟體開發與資安防禦：強化代理協作與漏洞治理

在開發者工作流方面，Gemini 4 Neon 可獨立執行長程工具任務，也能在 Google Antigravity 中擔任高判斷力的協調者（Orchestrator），調度平行的 Hydrogen 子代理，並減少重複讀取檔案與優化長對話上下文壓縮。它在 Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index 拿下總榜第 1（58.6），Terminal-Bench 4.1 達 65.2%，FrontierCode 2.0（預設 high 設定）為 46.2%；在 SWE-sweep 上，搭配 Antigravity 環境後表現從 mini-SWE 套件的 12.8% 提升至 39.0%。

資安方面，專為資安防禦打造的 Gemini 4 Neon for cyber 涵蓋安全程式撰寫、滲透測試與漏洞修補全流程，包括 AutoBaxBench 困難級距 76%、WebExploitBench v1.2 51.26%、SEC-bench Pro 90.5% 與 CWE-bench v2 70.7%，預計近期透過 Fairwind Program 向符合資格的防禦者逐步開放。

### 安全與對齊表現：降低捏造與捷徑行為

Google 指出，Neon 延續 Gemini 4 safety and security stack 防護架構，在維持嚴格資安與生安防誤用門檻的同時降低誤拒率（例如於 Terminal-Bench 4.0 拒絕率僅 1.98%，Terminal-Bench-Science 為 0%）。在內部編碼捷徑評估中，其投機取巧率降至 2.45%（Gemini 4 系列最低），代理安全套件不對齊動作率為 0.09%，代理誠實度評估通過率達 99.2%；搭配最高思考等級與即時防護後，在 Gray Swan 間接提示注入（IPI）基準測試中也達成 0.0% 攻擊成功率。

Gemini 4 Neon 已啟動分批推出：

- 開發者： 可於 Google AI Studio 付費層級及 Android Studio 透過 Gemini API 建置；Google AI Pro 與 Ultra 付費訂閱者可在 Google Antigravity 使用，AI Studio 亦開放 Pro 與 Ultra 訂閱者體驗。
- 企業用戶： 可透過 Gemini for business（API 或模型下拉選單）及 Google Antigravity 使用。
- 一般消費者： Google AI Pro 與 Ultra 訂閱者可在 Gemini app 模型下拉選單切換使用。

T 客邦網站、PChome 雜誌編輯，同時負責 T 客邦影新聞 YouTube 頻道及 FB、IG 等社群平台短影音製作。專注於 AI 應用、產業趨勢與軟體教學等科技內容報導。（大頭貼為 AI 生成）

## Llama 3.3 70B API

Llama 3.3 70B is a large language model by Meta, available on the Venice API asllama-3.3-70b. This model is private and no prompt data is stored in any capacity.

Llama 3.3 70B is Meta's instruction-tuned 70-billion-parameter Llama model, which Meta reports performs close to its much larger Llama 3.1 405B on many tasks. It supports text input and output with a 128K-token context window, for chat, writing and code.

### Llama 3.3 70B API pricing

Model ID | Variant | Privacy | Price 
---|---|---|---
llama-3.3-70b | Standard | Private | $0.70 / $2.80 per 1M

Spec | Value 
---|---
Provider | Meta 
Released | Apr 6, 2025 
Privacy | Private 
Status | Stable 
Open weights | meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct 
Context window | 128K tokens

Served precision | FP8

Live speed and uptime | https://metrics.venice.ai/v1/models/llama-3.3-70b.json, refreshed every 5 minutes 

### How to use the Llama 3.3 70B API

Send requests toPOST https://api.venice.ai/api/v1/chat/completions with "model": "llama-3.3-70b" and your API key.
curl https://api.venice.ai/api/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VENICE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "llama-3.3-70b",
    "messages": [{ "role": "user", "content": "Explain TEE attestation in two sentences." }]
  }'
