## India AI Mission-supported Chariot-1 Foundation Models Launched, Strengthening India's Indigenous AI Capabilities

### 
Developed in India through Indigenous Research, Chariot-1 Advances Multilingual Language Processing and Speech Generation with Innovations Tailored to India's Linguistic Diversity

Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 11:23AM by PIB Delhi

In a significant milestone towards strengthening India's indigenous Artificial Intelligence (AI) ecosystem, Shri S. Krishnan, Secretary, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), inaugurated the launch of Chariot-1 Foundation Models, developed by Chariot Artificial Intelligence Pvt. Ltd., under the IndiaAI Mission. The launch and research showcase took place at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, highlighting India's growing capability to develop sovereign AI technologies through homegrown research and innovation.

Chariot Artificial Intelligence Pvt. Ltd. is among the first four teams selected under the IndiaAI Mission to develop sovereign foundation models. The initiative reflects the Government of India's commitment to nurturing indigenous AI capabilities, supporting advanced research and enabling the development of AI models that address India's unique technological, linguistic and societal requirements.

The Chariot-1 model suite comprises Chariot-1 Large Language Model (LLM) and Chariot-1 Text-to-Speech (TTS), developed through pre-training from scratch in India. Designed to advance language understanding and speech generation, the models incorporate novel research innovations aimed at improving computational efficiency, multilingual capabilities and adaptability across different deployment environments.

Advancing Multilingual AI through Indigenous Research

A key highlight of the launch was the presentation of three research innovations developed by the Chariot team and integrated into the training of Chariot-1 models. These innovations address fundamental challenges in language processing and model training, particularly in the context of India's diverse linguistic landscape.

IndicShift, an open-source innovation, introduces a shared alphabet for Indian scripts, enabling AI models to leverage similarities across languages rather than treating each script independently. Covering 1,012 characters across 12 Indian scripts through 350 letters, the approach achieves up to 2.5 times fewer tokens on Indian text compared to OpenAI's GPT tokeniser. The research also reports a 5% to 8% improvement in model performance on Indian languages on the same compute, while maintaining performance in English and code.

Nested Training enables three complete model sizes to be trained simultaneously through a single training run and one set of weights. This innovation addresses the challenge of developing separate models for different computing environments, enabling deployment across data centres, laptops, smartphones and edge devices. The approach delivers a reported 62 % improvement in training speed compared to training the three model sizes separately.

The third innovation, Mixture of Vocabularies, optimises the model's word-selection process by dividing its vocabulary into 11 groups and scoring only the relevant group at a time. This approach reduces the number of vocabulary entries scored per word by 5.7 times and delivers a 38 % improvement in training speed on the same GPUs, with negligible change in model loss.

Chariot-1: Building AI for India's Multilingual Landscape

The Chariot-1 LLM is an 11-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model, with 4 billion active parameters per token. Pre-trained from scratch in India, it is available in three model sizes-10.7 billion, 1.7 billion and 745 million parameters-catering to varying computational requirements and deployment environments.

Complementing the language model, Chariot-1 TTS is designed to generate speech in English and 10 Indian languages: Hindi, Bengali, Marathi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Gujarati, Punjabi and Odia.

A distinctive capability of the speech model is its ability to understand context and determine how numbers, dates, currencies, units, URLs and abbreviations should be verbalised. This enables more natural and context-aware speech generation, addressing an important challenge in developing speech technologies for real-world applications.

The model recorded over 97% verbalisation accuracy on the Async TTS Pronunciation Benchmark, comprising 1,029 real-world sentences and 2,251 instances of non-standard text across 42 categories. It also achieved a Hindi character error rate of 7.60 % and an average character error rate of 6.47 % across nine other Indian languages, the lowest among the systems evaluated in the reported tests.

These developments demonstrate the importance of building language technologies that account for the complexities of Indian languages, supporting the broader objective of making AI more accessible and relevant across India's diverse linguistic communities.

Leadership Perspectives

Shri S. Krishnan, Secretary, MeitY, congratulated the Chariot team on the launch of Chariot One, describing it as a significant achievement for India’s technology ecosystem. He highlighted the team’s innovative approach, efficient use of Indian-language representation and its contribution to advancing indigenous AI capabilities. He noted that the IndiaAI Mission was designed to nurture and support such talent, and appreciated the contribution of the two Stanford graduates who chose to return to India to build advanced AI technology. He said that Chariot One exemplifies the potential of India’s young innovators and demonstrates the country’s growing capability to develop cutting-edge technologies.

The launch of Chariot-1 underscores the growing role of Indian AI enterprises in advancing indigenous foundation model development. Through the IndiaAI Mission, the Government of India is fostering a robust ecosystem for AI research, innovation and development, with a focus on building domestic capabilities and reducing dependence on externally developed technologies.

By supporting teams developing sovereign foundation models, the IndiaAI Mission is enabling researchers, innovators and enterprises to pursue ambitious AI research and translate it into homegrown technological solutions. Such initiatives are central to India's vision of building an inclusive, self-reliant and globally competitive AI ecosystem.

The event also featured a fireside conversation between Shri Vishal Dhupar, Managing Director, South Asia, NVIDIA, and Shri Suvrat Bhooshan, Co-Founder, Chariot, focusing on emerging developments in AI research and the evolving technology landscape.

These innovations address fundamental challenges in language processing and model training, particularly in the context of India's diverse linguistic landscape.

IndicShift, an open-source innovation, introduces a shared alphabet for Indian scripts, enabling AI models to leverage similarities across languages rather than treating each script independently. # 商汤发布SenseNova U1.6，赋能内部AI应用与外部多元创作场景

2026-11-24 19:12:31来源：央广网

11月24日，商汤科技正式发布并开源图像生成模型SenseNova U1.6。作为日日新大模型体系的重要组成部分，U1.6延续U系列理解与生成统一范式，首次为该系列8B开源模型引入原生图像自修正能力，在图像美学表现、文字生成准确性及复杂视觉内容创作方面实现升级。目前，其API服务版本SenseNova U1.6 Lite已接入商汤小浣熊、Seko、Kapi相机等产品，并通过开源及API服务向更广泛的开发者和用户开放，推动模型能力从技术研发走向更广泛的实际应用。

在大模型行业竞争从参数规模、榜单排名逐步走向应用落地的背景下，轻量化、场景化的模型能力正展现出新的发展空间。相较于持续追求模型规模与通用能力的竞争路径，小参数模型凭借部署灵活、调用成本及场景适配等优势，正在成为AI应用规模化落地的重要支撑。

在核心能力方面，SenseNova U1.6重点强化了美学表现与图像自修正两大能力。一方面，模型针对人像摄影、艺术插画、信息图等不同内容类型进行美学优化，能够更好地理解胶片质感、光影效果、艺术笔触及复杂排版等创作需求；另一方面，模型首次实现了原生图像自修正，能够在生成首稿后自主检查画面，对文字模糊、错字乱码、英文拼写错误及编号错乱等问题进行定位和修正，将“生成、检查、修改”融入同一次创作流程，减少用户反复调整和返工的时间成本。内部用户评测显示，U1.6 Lite美学得分较上一代U1.5 Lite提升约10%；在UltraTextBench密集信息图测试中，开启自修正后得分由86.04提升至92.28，相对提升约7%。

模型能力的升级正进一步转化为商汤产品端的用户价值。目前，SenseNova U1.6 Lite已接入商汤小浣熊、Seko、Kapi相机等产品。其中，商汤小浣熊面向日常办公场景，支持用户高效生成插画、海报及信息图，提升办公视觉内容生产效率；Seko聚焦短剧及影视内容创作，可为剧集视觉素材及影视内容资产制作提供模型支持，拓展AI在内容生产工作流中的应用空间；Kapi相机则探索生成式AI与影像创作的融合，为用户提供更多视觉表达和影像创作可能。

商汤内部已经形成的AI应用矩阵，为这一模型能力提供了现成的落地土壤。商汤小浣熊累计服务用户已超2000万，2026年Q3其Web端月独立访客数与使用时长居综合类套件第一；Seko的AI视频智能体及内容创编能力，与覆盖180个国家和地区、9000余个海外频道的发行运营网络相结合，为创作者打通AI内容出海商业化通路；咔皮系列累计用户突破5000万。

除内部产品矩阵外，SenseNova U1.6已正式开源模型权重，并上线ComfyUI等创作工具，同时通过SenseNova Token Plan提供API服务，使得模型可服务于更广泛的办公与创作场景。例如，用户可生成商务海报、信息图与营销物料；设计师和创作者可完成插画、人像风格化与社交媒体视觉内容；短剧及影视制作团队可用于视觉素材生产。从内部产品接入到外部开发者生态开放，商汤正推动模型能力向办公、内容生产及影像创作等多元场景延伸。

从模型发布到产品接入，再到创作工具生态拓展，商汤正在推动AI能力形成从底层模型到终端应用的落地链路。与此同时，资本市场对商汤的价值判断也在发生变化。今年以来，多家机构认为，商汤正从一家持续证明技术能力的公司，逐步迈向商业价值验证阶段。11月19日，申万宏源在研报中考虑到商汤Q3生成式AI收入增长加快、推理效率提升带动毛利改善，以及人员成本下降推动研发费用率大幅改善等因素，再次维持对商汤的买入评级。从模型技术迭代到应用场景拓展，再到经营效率与盈利能力改善，商汤的商业化进程正迎来多维度验证。

（注：此文属于央广网登载的商业信息，文章内容不代表本网观点，仅供参考。）

# Model Release Notes

Review OpenAI model releases, capability updates, retirements, and changes to the Model Spec.

Updated: 15小时前

# November 24, 2026

## Healthcare model configurations in the OpenAI API

Healthcare model configurations are now available in the OpenAI API. These configurations tailor models such as Astra and Sol for healthcare use cases. When web search is enabled, they can search a dedicated healthcare index to help developers build applications that find, compare, and summarize medical evidence with citations.

They’re available to API organizations through the Responses API. You don’t need a ChatGPT for Healthcare workspace to use them. These configurations do not replace professional medical judgment. For capabilities, availability, and requirements for handling protected health information, see: Healthcare model configurations in the OpenAI API.

# November 17, 2026

## GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol in the OpenAI API

We’re introducing GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol in the OpenAI API. Astra is our frontier model for applications that need advanced reasoning, coding, and the ability to handle complex professional work. Sol combines speed and lower cost with the ability to work through tasks that take several steps. Both improve on their predecessors’ results on demanding tasks while generating fewer output tokens.
Use gpt-6.2-astra or gpt-6.2-sol with the Responses or Chat Completions API. Both models accept text and images and return text, and review Standard API rates.

# November 16, 2026

## OpenAI CSAM image classifier

The OpenAI CSAM (Child Sexual Abuse Material) Image Classifier helps approved organizations review images for potential CSAM, including AI-generated material. Access is available through the OpenAI API at no cost and requires approval.

The classifier returns scores that can help trained reviewers prioritize review. It does not replace human judgment. Organizations remain responsible for reviewing results and deciding what action to take, including any reporting obligations.

Access requires an application, verification, program onboarding, and acceptance of the applicable terms. For application instructions, see: Requesting access to the OpenAI CSAM Image Classifier.

# October 30, 2026

## GPT-6 Rosalind Research

GPT-6 Rosalind Research brings GPT-6 reasoning capabilities to multistep life sciences research, with safeguards designed for biological work. It is rolling out to a limited set of approved Research customers in Work, Codex, and the API. It is not available in the Chat tab.

Access requires Rosalind Research approval for your organization and authorized users. Discovery approval does not grant Research access. Customers can continue to use GPT-5.5 Rosalind Research, and Rosalind Discovery remains on 5.5. On the API, usegpt-6-rosalind.

In Enterprise workspaces, the model starts in a two-week Admin Preview and is off by default. Admins can enable approved Research users and configure access for after the preview.

For access and setup, see: GPT-Rosalind for life sciences research. For pricing, see: API pricing, the credit-based rate card, or the Enterprise token-based rate card.

# October 29, 2026

## GPT-6 in ChatGPT update

We’re updating GPT-6 in Chat to give more concise responses and reduce overly flattering language. This update applies to Free and Go users, and people using ChatGPT without signing in.

On Plus and Pro, it applies only to the model ChatGPT can switch to after you reach GPT-6 message limits. The main GPT-6 model on Plus and Pro is unchanged.

## Updates to the OpenAI Model Spec

We’ve updated the Model Spec, our public description of how we want our models to behave. The revision reorganizes its guidance around five values: faithfulness to human intent, harm minimization, honesty and transparency, human agency, and care. It clarifies how GPT should understand human intent and exercise judgment in unfamiliar situations while remaining faithful to human direction and oversight.

Alongside clearer explanations of existing principles, the update adds guidance on context, memory, personalization, human agency, and oversight, and revises guidance on controlling and communicating side effects. It also adjusts some behavioral defaults and retires most detailed style guidance. Throughout the Spec, we now refer to the model as “GPT” rather than “the assistant,” reflecting its broader range of uses.

Read more about the changes and their rationale in our blog post, or explore the updated Model Spec.

# October 26, 2026

## GPT-6.1 Terra

GPT-6.1 Terra is rolling out in the OpenAI API as gpt-6.1-terra and in ChatGPT Work and Codex. It supports a range of tasks, including visual reasoning, computer use, and writing.

Standard API pricing is $1 per million input tokens, $0.05 per million cached input tokens, and $5 per million output tokens. API usage is billed separately from ChatGPT subscriptions.

In ChatGPT, Terra is available in Work and Codex, not Chat. It does not support UAE inference residency; this restriction is based on where inference runs, not your location.

For API capabilities and availability, see: Model directory. For help choosing a model in Work or Codex, see: Models.

# October 14, 2026

## Retiring GPT-5.5

We’re retiring GPT-5.5 from ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work, and Codex. This change does not affect API access.

# August 18, 2026

## Updates to the OpenAI Model Spec

We’ve updated the Model Spec, our living document outlining intended model behavior.

This update adds additional clarity around principles on appropriate relational interactions for teens. It also clarifies how assistants should handle false or unsupported premises, removes outdated guidance for pre-reasoning models, adds a new section "Be clear about capabilities and limits", and makes a few other small changes and copy edits.

More information on our principles related to teens can be found in our ChatGPT for Teens blog post, and the latest version of the Model Spec is available at model-spec.openai.com.

# July 9, 2026

## Introducing GPT-5.6 Sol in ChatGPT

We’re beginning the rollout of GPT-5.6 Sol in ChatGPT, our flagship reasoning model for complex work across coding, research, science, cybersecurity, computer use, and design.

GPT-5.6 Sol is rolling out to eligible paid ChatGPT plans. Free, Go, and logged-out users are not included. Availability may vary during rollout, and managed-workspace access can depend on administrator settings. Availability for other GPT-5.6 family models varies by product and plan; check the model picker or current rate card in the product you use.

# May 28, 2026

## GPT-5.5 Instant Update

We’re updating GPT-5.5 Instant in ChatGPT and the API to improve response style and quality. It’s now easier to read, more natural in everyday conversations, and better paced in practical help tasks, with fewer overly long or bullet-heavy responses.

With this update, canvas will no longer be available in GPT-5.5 Instant or GPT-5.5 Thinking. Writing and coding functionality is now supported directly in chat responses through writing blocks and code blocks. Paid users can continue using canvas for a limited time through legacy models until those models are sunset.

## Retiring OpenAI o3 and GPT-4.5

Today, we’re continuing to retire older models with limited usage in ChatGPT so we can better serve our newer, most capable models. OpenAI o3 will be retired from ChatGPT on August 26, 2026 following a 90-day sunset period, and GPT-4.5 will be retired from ChatGPT on June 27, 2026 following a 30-day sunset period. These models are currently available to paid users only via model settings. These changes apply to ChatGPT only; there are no changes to the API.

# March 18, 2026

## GPT-5.4 mini in ChatGPT

We’re rolling out GPT-5.4 mini in ChatGPT. GPT-5.4 mini is available to Free and Go users via the “Thinking” feature in the + menu. For all other users, GPT-5.4 mini is available as a rate limit fallback for GPT-5.4 Thinking.

For Plus, Pro, and other paid users, GPT-5.4 mini will be used as a fallback for GPT-5.4 Thinking when rate limits are reached, helping with continued access to reasoning capabilities during high usage. Enterprise customers will retain the option to default Auto routing to GPT-5.4 mini, if preferred.

GPT-5.4 mini will not appear as a selectable model in the model picker, and GPT-5 Thinking mini will be retired as a selectable option in 30 days. Learn more in our blog post.

# March 16, 2026

## GPT-5.3 Instant update

We’re rolling out an update to GPT-5.3 Instant that improves follow-up tone and reduces teaser-style phrasing in responses (e.g., “If you want…”, “You’ll never believe…”, “I can tell you these three things that…”).

# March 11, 2026

## Retiring GPT-5.1 models

As of March 11, 2026, GPT-5.1 models are no longer available in ChatGPT.

This applies to GPT-5.1 Instant, GPT-5.1 Thinking, and GPT-5.1 Pro. Existing conversations that used GPT-5.1 will automatically continue on the corresponding current model: GPT-5.3 Instant, GPT-5.4 Thinking, or GPT-5.4 Pro.

# March 5, 2026

## GPT-5.4 Thinking in ChatGPT

GPT‑5.4 brings together the best of our recent advances in reasoning, coding, and agentic workflows into a single frontier model. It incorporates the industry-leading coding capabilities of GPT‑5.3‑Codex while improving how the model works across tools, software environments, and professional tasks involving spreadsheets, presentations, and documents. The result is a model that gets complex real work done accurately, effectively, and efficiently—delivering what you asked for with less back and forth.

# Krafton Releases In-House AI Model Raon-1 Mini

## Open-source model reduces inference costs and outperforms six overseas peers in instruction-following tests

Krafton released the full version of its internally developed large language model (LLM), Raon-1 mini, on Nov. 25.

According to the company, Raon-1 mini is an artificial intelligence (AI) model developed entirely in-house, from model architecture design to training. It adopts a mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture that activates only 4 billion of its 30 billion parameters for computation. Combined with Krafton’s proprietary linear attention technology, the architecture improves response speed and reduces inference costs.

Krafton said the full version offers improved reasoning and complex task execution capabilities compared with the preview version. It scored 64.9 on MultiChallenge, a benchmark measuring a model’s ability to follow user instructions and constraints across multiple conversational turns, up 5.9 points from the preview version. According to Krafton, the model outperformed all six comparable overseas models.

The model also scored 72.3 and 55.9 on GDPval and BrowseComp Plus, respectively, which evaluate AI agents’ task execution capabilities. It achieved the highest scores among comparable MoE models in both benchmarks.

Krafton also added adjustable reasoning capabilities. Users can select from six reasoning levels depending on task complexity. The model answers simple questions without a reasoning process while allocating more computational resources to complex tasks.

Krafton released Raon-1 mini on AI model-sharing platform Hugging Face under the Apache 2.0 license. Anyone can download the model for free and use it for research and commercial service development. The company also provides an environment for testing the model and an application programming interface (API).

Since launching its AI model brand Raon in April, Krafton has released open-source AI models for speech and vision applications. The company plans to introduce Raon-1, a larger model than Raon-1 mini, and a real-time bidirectional speech model capable of listening and responding to users simultaneously.

# Lumivero launches POLI AI agents for portfolio planning
Wed, 25th Nov 2026 (Today) 
JOSEPH GABRIEL LAGONSIN News Editor

Lumivero has launched POLI, a new family of AI agents in its SharpCloud platform for portfolio project management and strategic roadmapping.

POLI is aimed at organisations managing complex project portfolios, particularly in defence, energy, manufacturing and government. It works with existing portfolio, project and risk data in SharpCloud and is intended to help analysts, risk managers and executives identify projects under pressure, test scenarios and assess the impact of decisions before they are made.

Portfolio focus

SharpCloud already combines strategy, project and risk data in a single model. POLI builds on that structure by letting users query the portfolio in plain language and review the knock-on effects of changes across programmes without waiting for a reporting cycle.

Users can turn an existing spreadsheet into a portfolio view, create calculations and views through plain-language prompts, ask questions of portfolio data, simulate changes across the portfolio and trace links between projects, risks and commitments.

As data changes, the model recalculates to give different users access to the same underlying facts. Any proposed change must be approved by a person before it is applied, and changes can be reversed.

The launch comes as companies continue to look for ways to use AI in capital project decision-making while maintaining tighter control over risk and governance. Lumivero cited research showing that fragmented data was the leading challenge for 81% of respondents in a study on AI in capital project decision-making.

The same research found that only 10% of respondents would act on an AI recommendation without significant review, while 56% cited data privacy and security as a leading buyer concern. According to Lumivero, SharpCloud does not use customer data to train models, and POLI cannot exceed a user's existing permissions.

Customers can run POLI on their own large language model or use one supplied by Lumivero. The agents can also be configured around an organisation's own projects, risk frameworks and terminology.

Gareth Morrison, Chief Executive Officer of Lumivero, said the product was intended to address a gap between information and action for organisations running large project portfolios.

"Organisations running complex project portfolios aren't short on data. They're short on answers," Morrison said. "POLI closes the gap between the data and the decision. It does the digging and the analysis, so leaders can focus on what matters most: making the calls that deliver the most value from every dollar invested."

SharpCloud is already used by organisations managing programmes where changes to dates, budgets or suppliers can affect wider commitments. In such settings, Lumivero argues, static reporting can leave decision-makers working from outdated information.

The Denver-headquartered group operates across the Americas, EMEA and APAC, providing research and decision software to customers in sectors including academia, industrials, energy, financial services, life sciences and manufacturing. Its tools are used by thousands of organisations to analyse large volumes of data, manage projects and support scientific research output.

A long-term SharpCloud user in the defence and space sector described the new tool positively in a G2 review, calling it "a game changer when integrating your roadmaps to gain insights and support decision making".

cross_cutting.title: Sona8 launches AI voice agents for staff interviews
cross_cutting.description: Sona8 launches AI voice agents for staff interviews ... Sona8 has launched AI voice agents that interview employees across entire organisations. The startup says it has conducted more than 10,000 interviews for over 20 organisations.
cross_cutting.content:
IT Brief Australia - Technology news for CIOs & IT decision-makers

# Sona8 launches AI voice agents for staff interviews
Thu, 26th Nov 2026 (Today) 
SEAN MITCHELL Publisher

Sona8 has launched AI voice agents that interview employees across entire organisations. The startup says it has conducted more than 10,000 interviews for over 20 organisations.

The San Francisco-based company, part of Y Combinator's Fall 2026 batch, runs interviews by phone or in a web browser and supports conversations in a worker's own language.

The product is designed to address a problem many large employers face when making decisions on restructurings, AI deployments and other internal changes. Traditional surveys can gather answers at scale but often reduce views to numerical scores. Conventional interviews provide more detail but usually reach only a small sample of staff.

Each interview with Sona8's voice agent lasts between 10 and 20 minutes. Managers then receive reported themes, the number of people who raised each issue and the exact sentences linked to each theme.

This allows organisations to trace findings back to what workers actually said rather than relying only on survey aggregates. They can also repeat the process after taking action to compare changes in sentiment or concerns.

The founders said the idea emerged from work on a transformation project in Hamburg, as they considered how companies gather feedback during large-scale change programmes. Anton Hantel and Thilo Tamme questioned why AI could not be used to extend interviews beyond a few dozen people to an entire workforce.

Adoption so far has centred on organisations in Germany, Austria, the Nordics and the United States. Consulting teams at one of the three largest strategy consultancies already use the system for stakeholder interviews and diagnostics, according to the company.

In one deployment, 87.5% of invited participants took part, Sona8 said. In that project, 400 interviews identified 35 AI use cases and 13 barriers.

Interview model

The approach includes workers without desks or company laptops by allowing interviews over the phone. That could widen access for frontline staff, who are often harder to reach through browser-based tools or internal office software.

Sona8 said its agents can ask follow-up questions based on what a person says during the conversation. It argues this makes the process closer to a conventional interview than a scripted survey.

Research has become part of the company's pitch to customers and partners. Sona8 said it is testing its method with researchers at the Technical University of Munich and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.

It added that seven papers written with those researchers were accepted this year at the European Conference on Information Systems, the Strategic Management Society Conference and the Hawaii International Conference on System Sciences. The topics include whether positive survey ratings can obscure employee concerns and how large language models affect which employee views are retained in summaries.

Privacy focus

The startup said it designed the product around European data protection rules and works council requirements. It said those constraints shaped the system from the outset and that the product is GDPR-compliant.

That focus may matter for multinational employers operating in markets where employee consultation and data handling are tightly regulated. Workplace listening tools have come under scrutiny in Europe over how organisations collect, process and act on staff feedback.

Sona8 was founded by Chief Executive Officer Anton Hantel, Chief Technology Officer Madeleine Malmsten and Chief Product Officer Thilo Tamme. The company is based in San Francisco.

"Most organisations only hear from the people who fill in a survey, or from the few dozen who get an interview," said Thilo Tamme, Co-Founder and Chief Product Officer at Sona8.

"When everyone can talk for ten or twenty minutes in their own language, leaders hear what is really going on, and they can check every finding against the words people actually used," Tamme said.

cross_cutting.title: Luma launches AI agent hub for patient procedure prep
cross_cutting.description: Luma launches AI agent hub for patient procedure prep Wed, 25th Nov 2026 (Yesterday) ... Luma Health has launched Agent Launchpad for healthcare systems, a product designed to manage AI agents that prepare patients for procedures and follow up afterwards.
cross_cutting.content:
IT Brief UK - Technology news for CIOs & IT decision-makers

# Luma launches AI agent hub for patient procedure prep
Wed, 25th Nov 2026 (Yesterday) 
SEAN MITCHELL Publisher

Luma Health has launched Agent Launchpad for healthcare systems, a product designed to manage AI agents that prepare patients for procedures and follow up afterwards.

The first rollout covers colonoscopy preparation and follow-up, knee replacement preparation, cataract surgery preparation, bariatric surgery preparation, endoscopy preparation and pain management guidance. The system contacts patients by phone call and text message, follows each health system's protocol and passes clinical issues to nursing teams.

The product is intended to handle routine pre-procedure conversations that often take up nursing time. These exchanges can include questions about whether patients have obtained preparation supplies, followed medication instructions and have a history of problems with anaesthesia.

Patients can respond in their own words at any time of day. If a patient raises a clinical concern, the system sends the conversation to the relevant care team so staff can take over with the prior context.

Two healthcare providers, the University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences and Mile Bluff Medical Centre, are already using the system for colonoscopy preparation. According to figures released by Luma, patients who received outreach recorded an average response rate of 95%, with 70% responding within the first day.

At Mile Bluff, half of patients completed their procedure preparation without any staff phone calls, according to Luma. The company also said perioperative nurses saved more than 20 minutes of coordination time per patient on average.

Staff workload

Procedure preparation has become a significant administrative burden for care teams because staff often need to repeat the same instructions to large numbers of patients and make several attempts before reaching them. Luma's approach is to automate those routine exchanges while keeping nurses involved when clinical judgement is required.

This is particularly important for services such as colonoscopy, where providers want to reduce missed or poorly prepared appointments. If patients do not complete the required steps in advance, hospitals and clinics can lose procedure time and may need to reschedule patients.

Paige Anderson, Assistant Clinical Service Manager at UAMS, described the impact on nursing staff and patients.

"Our nurses historically spent a large part of their day on the phone, walking patients through their prep, what medications to hold and general questions regarding their upcoming procedure. Many of our patients travel a great distance for these procedures, so understanding what is required and being prepared is key for a successful outcome for both the patient and organization. Luma's agentic procedure prep now answers routine prep questions for patients, day or night, at the times that work best for them. When a question needs a nurse, it comes straight to our team. Patients are completing their prep and showing up ready, and our nurses have more time for the clinical work only they can do," said Anderson.

Tamara Coughlin, Director of Surgery at Mile Bluff Medical Centre, said the system had reduced the number of preparation calls handled by nurses.

"It's important to get as many patients through our doors as we can to keep their preventive care on track. But with complex procedures like colonoscopies, patients often have multiple steps to complete and need guidance from our perioperative team. Luma's agentic procedure prep has reduced the number of hours our nurses spend making preparation calls by allowing patients to ask questions whenever it's convenient for them. We're seeing more patients prepared for their procedures earlier, with less burden on staff," said Coughlin.

Broader push

The launch adds to a wider effort by healthcare technology suppliers to use AI tools for operational tasks rather than direct diagnosis. Here, the emphasis is on patient communication, readiness tracking and routing exceptions to clinicians, rather than replacing clinical decision-making.

Luma describes Agent Launchpad as a single place for health systems to run AI agents that manage multistep workflows from start to finish. The current release focuses on procedure preparation and post-procedure checks, where repeated outreach and standard instructions make automation easier to deploy.

Based in San Francisco, Luma serves more than 1,000 healthcare organisations and says its systems reach more than 100 million patients across the US, UK and the Caribbean. The company also has research and development centres in the US, Brazil and Europe.

The latest data from UAMS and Mile Bluff suggest health systems are testing whether AI-led outreach can improve response rates while reducing the time nursing teams spend on routine coordination.

cross_cutting.content:
# AI agent Muse launches in UK to 'do your Christmas shopping' and pay bills

## An AI "agent" for tech giant and Facebook owner Meta has gone live in the UK - but it begs questions for businesses and regulators

Tech giant Meta has launched an AI agent in the UK which can read your emails, make purchases online and even pay bills.

Called Muse, it's billed as a tool to help with life admin, whether that be shopping, booking cinema tickets and even cancel your gym membership.

"From doing the Christmas shopping and searching for a cheaper energy deal, to sorting the school calendar. Muse can get it done for you," declared US goliath Meta as it launched the tool here. Meta also owns Facebook. Instagram and WhatsApp.

Supermarket giant Sainsbury's says its customers can already use Muse to help plan their weekly online shop and build a basket around their budget or meal plan. "Muse shops just as a customer would", the chain said.

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

Debenhams is another involved at the start, with shoppers' Muse agent able to browse the online department store's website and present a selection based on what it thinks they' would like, and buy anything on their behalf. Other UK companies using Muse in a similar way include Marks & Spencer, ASOS, Currys, easyJet and Jet2.

However, its launch here - after several countries around the world - has left businesses and regulators are grappling with its potential consequences.

Paul Arnold, head of the Information Commission's Office, said "privacy must be built into consumer-facing agentic products from the outset. We have been clear with Meta about its responsibilities under data protection law prior to launch."

The UK launch of Muse follows the US, Australia, Canada, Japan, Mexico and Singapore. When it went live in the US in September, it quickly became the most downloaded app on Apple’s App Store as users flocked to make use of its features.

The idea of AI agents is that they go beyond answering questions that people type into a computer or phone but actually carry out tasks. Meta has given the examples of "searching for a cheaper energy deal" or "sorting the school calendar."

The roll-out of Muse is important to billionaire Mark Zuckerberg's Meta, as the US tech heavyweight has invested a fortune developing it.

"It doesn't just answer questions, it actually goes out and does work for you," said David Singleton, Meta's VP of engineering on AI products. "So it helps people stay on top of things," he added. "(It) helps you take tasks and projects off your plate, and also helps you turn your long-term goals into action plans."

The ICO's Paul Arnold said: "Agentic AI has significant potential to benefit people and businesses, from saving time on everyday tasks to driving innovation and growth across the economy. For people to benefit from these technologies with confidence, privacy must be built into consumer-facing agentic products from the outset.

"We have been clear with Meta about its responsibilities under data protection law prior to launch, particularly the requirement to ensure that users and the wider public can meaningfully understand and control how their personal data is used in the Muse product.

"Meta has committed to a voluntary monitoring and reporting scheme with the ICO to ensure we can scrutinise the technology, the user experience and feedback as it is developing. Like any organisation developing or deploying AI agents, Meta is responsible for ensuring that its products fully comply with UK data protection law."

Sarah Cardell, chief executive of the Competition and Markets Authority, said: “The CMA has been clear that UK consumer protection law applies to AI products. The CMA has engaged with Meta over the past few weeks ahead of the launch of Muse. As a result, they have made changes to their terms and conditions to make them fairer. We now need to examine carefully how Muse actually works in practice. We will be closely monitoring this and if we have concerns we will not hesitate to act to protect UK consumers. “

Article continues below

She added: “While suppliers of AI agents must act responsibly and comply with the law, we would also encourage users to consider carefully both the risks and benefits. While the agent may be designed to work on its own, users should review what that means in practice, how much autonomy they want to allow and check their permissions and approvals are set according to the risks they are prepared to accept.”

cross_cutting.description: Meta launches Muse in UK – the AI agent that can do your Christmas shopping ... Mark Zuckerberg’s Meta is launching its Muse AI assistant in the UK and is encouraging users to let it loose on your apps – and the high street. ... booking travel or buying festive presents.
cross_cutting.content:
# Meta launches Muse in UK – the AI agent that can do your Christmas shopping

Users can give agents tasks such as booking travel or buying presents, but glitches have been reported

Want to avoid the Christmas shopping hordes? Then let your AI agent do the shopping for you. Mark Zuckerberg’s Meta is launching its Muse AI assistant in the UK and is encouraging users to let it loose on your apps – and the high street.

Muse has been a hit in the US and is ranked first and second respectively on Google and Apple’s free app stores, having been downloaded millions of times. However, UK regulators have said they are keeping a close eye on the launch over privacy and consumer protection requirements.

Muse can be used as an app or directly within Meta’s WhatsApp messaging platform. Meta invites users to give their assistant a name, a look and a personality, so they can talk to it as well as assign it tasks such as sending an email, booking travel or buying festive presents.

“From doing the Christmas shopping and searching for a cheaper energy deal, to sorting the school calendar … Muse can get it done for you,” Meta said.

The company acknowledged that handing control of your day-to-day digital life to an AI agent was “an act of trust”. Muse cannot make a purchase or send an email without your permission and will only be connected to apps that you let it join.

The app has no visibility into people’s passwords or payment methods, Meta said, and it does not share your conversations with advertisers. It will ask for your approval before making a purchase or sending an email, while a separate “security agent” checks Muse’s actions against the permissions you’ve granted.

“Think of it as a helping hand for the jobs that pile up, like chasing a refund, renewing car insurance or keeping on top of the school calendar,” Meta said. “To get those jobs done, you can connect Muse to the apps you already use, from your email and calendar to the retailer apps you shop on.”

Meta said it had signed deals with an array of British businesses – including Marks & Spencer, Currys, Sainsbury’s and easyJet – allowing Muse to navigate their websites more easily and to access their apps. If a company does not offer a “connector” app that Muse can visit, the agent will access their website instead.

The Information Commission’s Office and the Competition and Markets Authority said they had been in talks with Meta ahead of the launch about its responsibility to comply with UK laws. The ICO, the UK’s data protection watchdog, said on Tuesday that Meta had committed to a “voluntary monitoring and reporting scheme” with the regulator, while the CMA said talks with Meta had resulted in changes to make the app’s terms and conditions “fairer”.

“We will be closely monitoring this and if we have concerns we will not hesitate to act to protect UK consumers,” said Sarah Cardell, the CMA chief executive.

Reuters reported last week that Meta employees had raised concerns about the app’s performance, including one staff member receiving a reminder to respond to a message from her sister on Signal, an encrypted messaging app. In another example reported by Reuters, Muse delivered a message with random bank account balances in it.

Meta said internal testing was vital for product development and allowed the company to implement safety and privacy protection before releasing anything publicly. It is understood the majority of problems flagged by Reuters related to a bug that has been fixed.

Muse is powered by Muse Spark, Meta’s first model from the company’s “super intelligence” AI lab. In a social media post on Sunday, Meta’s chief AI officer, Alexandr Wang, raised the possibility of humanity losing control over AI systems that are able to improve themselves autonomously.

“It is … hard to imagine a world where humanity maintains control with super intelligence that is 1000x smarter and more capable than humans in every field,” he wrote.

Responding to reports that AI had cracked one of the most important unsolved problems in mathematics – the Riemann hypothesis – Wang said the tech industry needed to make progress in the “extremely urgent” areas of AI safety, security and alignment. Alignment refers to ensuring an AI system adheres to human goals and values.

cross_cutting.content:
# Stratum Holdings and Ocean Power Technologies partner on offshore data centers

Companies are exploring viability of data centers powered by renewable wave, wind, and solar energy

Stratum Holdings and Ocean Power Technologies (OPT) have signed an agreement to explore the development of offshore data centers powered by renewable wave, wind, and solar energy.

The two companies are set to begin the first phase of their joint work, looking into defined work on combining OPT’s PowerBuoy technology with Stratum’s high-performance GPU infrastructure, including Nvidia B300 GPUs.

OPT's PowerBuoy is a platform that delivers renewable power and real-time data communications for remote maritime and subsea applications

OPT will conduct a comprehensive technical and commercial feasibility assessment to evaluate the potential for deploying Stratum’s GPU infrastructure on its PowerBuoy platforms, including power generation and storage requirements, thermal management, communications capabilities, platform integration, and potential deployment locations.

The first phase of the partnership covers feasibility and planning only, and does not include equipment fabrication, GPU integration, offshore deployment, or at-sea testing. Industries targeted by the platform include defense and security, oil and gas, environmental monitoring, and scientific exploration.

“This agreement takes our collaboration with OPT from a letter of intent to defined work, with a path toward a demonstration at sea,” said Nicholas H. Adler, CEO of Stratum Holdings. “Demand for AI computing is growing faster than the power and cooling available on land, and the industry is beginning to look offshore. We believe pairing our Nvidia B300 GPUs with OPT’s PowerBuoy platform, which generates its own renewable power in a natural cooling environment, could give Stratum a differentiated position in this emerging market. The feasibility assessment is designed to give us the technical and commercial roadmap to pursue it.”

“Advancing into this initial phase allows us to take a more detailed look at the technical and commercial requirements for combining our PowerBuoy technology with Stratum’s GPU infrastructure,” added Tracy Pagliara, acting president and CEO of Ocean Power Technologies. “Our focus will be on evaluating the power, thermal management, and communications capabilities necessary to support offshore AI computing and establishing a foundation for a potential demonstration program.”

Stratum was formerly a real estate business and was named La Rosa Holdings Corp., but sold off its legacy real estate operations earlier this month to focus on its AI cloud business. In October, Stratum acquired Nvidia B300 GPUs and placed them under a long-term leasing arrangement designed to generate recurring revenue. It is unclear what scale the cluster is operating at. The company is headquartered in Celebration, Florida.

Several companies are exploring the possibility of floating data centers. Optimal Transit has pitched a "Kraaken" floating data center that is self-powered. Keppel has started work on a 25MW floating facility in Singapore, due to come online in 2028, while US-based Panthalassa wants to harness the power of waves for floating data centers at sea.

Floating wind firm Aikido has also announced its entrance into the data center space with the launch of a floating offshore wind platform integrated with a modular AI-focused data center. Other companies working on floating projects include Seatrium, Mocean, and Atomarine.

DCD has covered the concept in detail in its magazine. Read more here

# Neysa Builds Enterprise Partner Network to Deploy AI Applications on Velocis

The programme will allow software companies, system integrators, and technology providers to build and deploy enterprise AI solutions on Neysa’s Velocis platform.

## Key takeaways

- Neysa has launched a partner programme to facilitate AI application development on its Velocis platform.
- The programme targets software companies, system integrators, and technology providers to enhance enterprise AI solutions.
- Neysa offers computing capacity, technical support, and access to sales teams to assist partners in solution development.
- The initiative aims to promote shared AI adoption opportunities across the ecosystem.
- Neysa is actively expanding its AI infrastructure to support growing customer demands.

Mumbai-based AI cloud infrastructure company Neysa has launched a partner programme to help build and deploy applications on its Velocis AI cloud platform, using Neysa's infrastructure to meet customers' computing requirements.

Neysa Partner Programme targets software companies, system integrators and resellers, consulting firms, and technology providers working across components such as networking, storage and computing. The company will provide computing capacity, technical support, deal registration, joint proposal development, and access to its sales teams to help partners develop solutions and pursue enterprise opportunities.

Neysa hopes to reach more customers with its infrastructure-as-a-service offering.

“This programme gives them a structured way to build solutions, pursue opportunities together and grow their AI businesses. The aim is to make enterprise AI adoption a shared opportunity across the ecosystem,” Aniket Chandavarkar, Head of Partner GTM, Neysa, said in a statement.

Mushtaq Khot, Director and Chief Revenue Officer at Lauren Group, a partner in the programme, said customers moving AI workloads from pilots to production need such solutions that make business sense without compromising control over data.

Neysa, meanwhile, continues to expand its own AI infrastructure footprint.

Earlier in November, it announced that an 8,192-GPU cluster powered by AMD Instinct MI350X accelerators had become operational in Mumbai. It is also preparing a deployment at STT Noida 2, designed to support up to 9,000 GPUs in its first phase. The project is expected to go live in the first quarter of calendar year 2027 and will support AI training and inference workloads for Indian enterprises and global customers.

In February, Neysa raised $600 million in equity funding from Blackstone and co-investors. The company intends to secure another $600 million in debt financing, subject to documentation, taking the proposed capital raise to $1.2 billion. The funding supported its deployment of more than 20,000 GPUs in India.

# Neysa launches partner programme to expand enterprise AI deployments in India

The programme will address the challenges enterprises face in moving AI projects from pilots to production, including integration with existing systems, security, workflow compatibility and ongoing operational support.

AI cloud infrastructure company Neysa has launched a partner programme to help AI product companies, system integrators, resellers, consulting firms and technology providers build and deliver AI solutions for enterprises across India.

The Neysa partner programme will bring together the company's AI cloud infrastructure, partners' applications and industry expertise, and enterprise integration capabilities to accelerate AI adoption. Partners will be able to develop solutions on Neysa Velocis, pursue joint customer opportunities and build services businesses around enterprise AI deployments.

It will address the challenges enterprises face in moving AI projects from pilots to production, including integration with existing systems, security, workflow compatibility and ongoing operational support.

“Neysa provides the AI infrastructure. Our partners bring the applications, industry knowledge and delivery expertise that turn it into business value. This programme gives them a structured way to build solutions, pursue opportunities together and grow their AI businesses. The aim is to make enterprise AI adoption a shared opportunity across the ecosystem,” said Aniket Chandavarkar, Head of Partner GTM, Neysa.

The programme has four partnership categories covering independent software vendors and solution providers, system integrators and resellers, advisory and consulting firms, and technology providers. The categories are designed to support application development, implementation, integration, managed services and joint technology architectures.

Neysa will provide partners with deal registration, access to its Partner Portal, technical and sales enablement, marketing resources and joint proposal development. Its Premier Tier will offer additional support for partners investing in joint solutions and market development.

“A pilot only has to work. In production, it has to make business sense without losing control over data. That is where our customers need us most, and with an AI Cloud provider like Neysa, we can walk that road with confidence,” Mushtaq Khot, Director and Chief Revenue Officer, Lauren Group, said.

Neysa said applications are open to AI product companies, software firms, system integrators, resellers and technology providers.

cross_cutting.content:
# Minfy and AWS expand global cloud and AI collaboration

## The five-year agreement expands the companies' collaboration beyond India and the US, with a focus on deploying industry-specific AI platforms and cloud services for enterprises.

New Update

Minfy, an applied AI and technology services company, has signed a five-year global Strategic Collaboration Agreement (SCA) with Amazon Web Services (AWS), extending their partnership until 2031. The agreement expands the scope of their existing collaboration from India and the US to global markets, reflecting growing enterprise demand for cloud infrastructure and AI-led services.

According to Minfy, the new agreement is three times the size of the target set under its previous SCA with AWS, signed in March 2024. Under the expanded arrangement, the companies will jointly develop and take industry-specific cloud and AI solutions to market, focusing on enterprise adoption across multiple sectors.

The collaboration will cover manufacturing and industrials, aerospace and satellite, media and entertainment, financial services and insurance, logistics, healthcare and the public sector. The focus will be on developing AI-enabled industry platforms using AWS cloud and AI services, including Amazon Bedrock and AWS Quick.

The agreement comes as enterprises move from experimenting with generative AI to deploying applications across business operations. According to McKinsey's 2026 global survey on AI, nearly nine in ten organisations use AI regularly in at least one business function, but around two-thirds have yet to scale its deployment across their enterprises.

This gap highlights the infrastructure and operational requirements associated with enterprise AI adoption. Beyond access to AI models, organisations need cloud computing capacity, data integration, application development capabilities, security and governance frameworks to deploy and manage AI systems at scale.

## Industry-specific AI Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure

As part of the agreement, Minfy will expand its portfolio of industry-specific platforms in global markets. These include mVISTA for autonomous information technology (IT) and operational technology (OT) operations, mPRISMA for agentic AI applications in media, and its Customer Data Platform for financial services.

The platforms are built on AWS's AI and cloud ecosystem, including Amazon Bedrock and AWS Quick, which support the development of AI agents, analytics and automation applications.

The collaboration will combine AWS's cloud infrastructure and AI services with Minfy's application development and implementation capabilities. The objective is to help enterprises integrate AI applications into existing business systems and operational workflows.

For enterprises, this involves more than deploying AI models. Integrating AI with operational technology, enterprise applications and data platforms requires reliable cloud infrastructure, secure data exchange, computing resources and governance mechanisms. These requirements are particularly relevant in sectors such as manufacturing, logistics and aerospace, where AI applications may interact with operational systems and business-critical processes.

Commenting on the agreement, Vijay Jain, founder and director of Minfy, said the companies had exceeded the objectives of their 2024 collaboration ahead of schedule. He attributed the expanded agreement to investments in leadership, data and AI capabilities, corporate governance and delivery infrastructure over the past two years.

Sandeep Dutta, president of AWS India and South Asia, said the expanded partnership would extend Minfy's AWS capabilities beyond India and the US. He added that the development of industry platforms using Amazon Bedrock and AWS Quick would support enterprises in moving AI applications from proof-of-concept stages into operational deployments.

## Cloud Infrastructure and Enterprise Digital Transformation

The companies' collaboration also reflects the growing role of cloud service providers and technology partners in implementing enterprise AI systems. While cloud platforms provide access to computing, storage, networking and AI services, implementation partners help organisations integrate these capabilities with existing infrastructure and business applications.

Indus Towers, one of Minfy's customers, cited the company's role in supporting its digital transformation programme. Neeti Wahi, chief digital and information officer at Indus Towers, said Minfy had worked with its digital and IT teams to develop a more scalable and secure platform foundation supporting nationwide operations and AI initiatives.

For telecom infrastructure providers such as Indus Towers, these capabilities are relevant to managing geographically distributed operations, integrating enterprise data and supporting the digital systems required for network infrastructure management.

Minfy currently operates 10 offices globally, including three delivery and centre of excellence hubs in Hyderabad, Gurugram and Virginia.

The company has also developed enterprise AI frameworks, including EGIRA (Enterprise General Intelligence Reference Architecture), designed to support the integration, scalability and governance of enterprise AI systems. Its mTRUST7 framework establishes a seven-pillar governance model for developing and operating customer systems.

The expanded agreement places greater emphasis on taking these capabilities to international markets. As enterprises increase investments in AI and cloud platforms, the ability to integrate computing infrastructure, data systems, networking and governance will remain central to deploying AI applications across business operations.

For India's cloud and enterprise technology ecosystem, the partnership also highlights the role of domestic technology services providers in taking AI implementation and cloud engineering capabilities to global markets.

# VAST Data Unveils VAST Takeoff, a Global Initiative To Launch, Scale and Support AI Cloud Providers

November 24, 2026

New launchpad offers cloud providers free access to VAST’s AI Operating System software and benefits to scale AI services.

Remote-First-Company | NEW YORK CITY – November 24, 2026 – VAST Data, the AI Operating System company, today announced VAST Takeoff, the industry’s first and only AI cloud launchpad designed to help every cloud easily build scalable cloud offerings and robust data services for the next generation of AI applications.

Supporting nearly 5 million GPUs, the VAST AI Operating System is the platform of choice for the world’s leading AI cloud providers. Today, Takeoff brings the benefits enjoyed by leading AI hyperscalers and extends them across the market to new and established clouds alike. Benefits include:

- Free VAST AI OS Software: Qualifying providers receive free access to the full VAST AI OS, with flexible entitlements ranging from 5 petabytes (PB) for one year to 1 PB for five years – or customized options in between. The offer can support new deployments or larger commercial agreements, freeing capital for GPUs, power, and customer acquisition.
- Availability-Backed Service Provider SLAs: VAST’s standardized availability commitments for service providers guarantee 100% availability to give participating AI clouds greater confidence and dedicated support as they bring enterprise workloads online.
- Joint Marketing and Business Development Support: Takeoff also offers qualifying providers potential opportunities for joint marketing initiatives, and assistance sourcing working capital and customer offtake, helping providers attract customers and grow their businesses.

“Building an AI cloud requires an enormous investment in infrastructure before the first customer ever comes online, and that capital pressure can limit who gets to participate in this market,” said Jeff Denworth, Co-Founder of VAST Data. “We’ve spent years building the software foundation behind some of the world’s largest AI environments. With Takeoff, we’re making that same technology accessible to emerging providers, removing upfront software licensing costs and providing protections and resources for clouds to scale so they can focus on winning customers and growing their businesses. An AI cloud’s success is our success, and we want to help all providers extend the power of AI to new and established end users around the world.”
VAST is already working with an initial group of emerging AI cloud providers, including Starcloud, to support the development of differentiated AI infrastructure services.
“Building AI infrastructure in space requires us to rethink nearly every aspect of the traditional data center,” said Adi Oltean, Chief Technology Officer at Starcloud. “VAST gives us a proven data foundation that can grow with our ambitions, while Takeoff allows us to direct more capital toward developing the infrastructure that makes space-based AI computing possible. Having a partner invested in our success makes a meaningful difference as we scale.”
Takeoff is available immediately, with applications now open to qualifying AI cloud providers. Participants are responsible for purchasing compatible hardware through VAST-authorized partners and covering deployment and installation costs. Participation is subject to VAST approval and program terms. Learn more and apply at Takeoff Launchpad.

## About VAST Data

VAST Data is the AI Operating System company – powering the next generation of intelligent systems with a unified software infrastructure stack that was purpose-built to unlock the full potential of AI. The VAST AI OS consolidates foundational data and compute services and agentic execution into one scalable platform, enabling organizations to deploy and facilitate communication between AI agents, reason over real-time data, and automate complex workflows at global scale. Built on VAST’s breakthrough DASE architecture – the world’s first true parallel distributed system architecture that eliminates tradeoffs between performance, scale, simplicity, and resilience – VAST has transformed its modern infrastructure into a global fabric for reasoning AI. Learn more at vastdata.com and follow VAST Data on LinkedIn, YouTube and X.
